title.zh: 卷一百九十六 列傳第一百二十一 隱逸
title.raw: 卷一百九十六 列傳第一百二十一 隱逸 Volume 196 Biographies 121: Recluses

sentences.zh: 古之隱者，大抵有三概：上焉者，身藏而德不晦，故自放草野，而名往從之，雖萬乘之貴，猶尋軌而委聘也；

translations.literal: Recluses of antiquity may be summed up in three general types. The highest type hides his person but does not obscure his virtue; therefore he releases himself to the wilds, and fame goes forth to follow him—even the honor of one who commands ten thousand chariots still seeks his track and entrusts him with an invitation.
translations.idiomatic: Recluses of old fell, broadly speaking, into three kinds. The highest kept themselves out of sight yet never let their virtue go dim; they roamed freely in field and thicket while reputation came to seek them out, and even rulers who commanded ten thousand chariots would trace their path and send formal invitations.

sentences.zh: 其次，挈治世具弗得伸，或持峭行不可屈於俗，雖有所應，其於爵祿也，泛然受，悠然辭，使人君常有所慕企，怊然如不足，其可貴也；

translations.literal: The next type carries the tools to order the age yet cannot extend them, or holds steep conduct that cannot be bent by custom; though he sometimes responds, toward rank and stipend he receives casually and declines at ease, so that the ruler always has something to admire and long for, vexed as though it were not enough—this is what makes him precious.
translations.idiomatic: The second sort bore the means to govern an age yet could not fully deploy them, or kept so steep a moral line that the world could not bend them; when they did respond to summons, they took titles and stipends lightly and let them go just as easily, leaving rulers forever yearning after them, restless as though something were still lacking—that was their worth.

sentences.zh: 末焉者，資槁薄，樂山林，內審其才，終不可當世取捨，故逃丘園而不返，使人常高其風而不敢加訾焉。

translations.literal: The lowest type has slender endowment, delights in mountains and forests, inwardly examines his talent and knows at last that he cannot meet the age's choices, so he flees to hill and garden and does not return, causing people always to exalt his air and not dare add reproach.
translations.idiomatic: The lowest had modest gifts, loved mountains and woods, and looked within until they knew their talents could never satisfy the world's demands; they withdrew to hill and garden and never came back, so that others always held their bearing in esteem and did not dare speak ill of them.

sentences.zh: 且世未嘗無隱，有之未嘗不旌賁而先焉者，以孔子所謂「舉逸民，天下之人歸焉」。

translations.literal: Moreover, the world has never lacked recluses; whenever there were such men, they were never not honored and placed first, as Confucius said, 'Raise up withdrawn subjects and the people of the realm will turn to you.'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the world has never been without recluses; whenever they appeared, courts honored them and put them first—just as Confucius said, 'Promote the withdrawn and the people will come to you.'

sentences.zh: 唐興，賢人在位眾多，其遁戢不出者，才班班可述，然皆下概者也。

translations.literal: When Tang rose, worthy men in office were many; those who hid and did not emerge, their talents can be set forth in ranks, yet all belonged to the lowest type.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang arose, the throne was full of able men; those who stayed in hiding nevertheless had talents worth recording, yet they all belonged to the lowest of the three types.

sentences.zh: 雖然，各保其素，非托默於語，足崖壑而志城闕也。

translations.literal: Even so, each kept his plain character; it was not feigned silence in speech, with feet in cliffs and gorges while the mind clung to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, each kept his native simplicity; this was not silence worn as a mask, with feet in ravines while the heart still yearned for court.

sentences.zh: 然放利之徒，假隱自名，以詭祿仕，肩相摩於道，至號終南、嵩少為仕途捷徑，高尚之節喪焉。

translations.literal: Yet men who sought profit borrowed the name of reclusion to gain office by deceit; they rubbed shoulders on the road until Zhongnan and Song-Shao were called shortcuts on the path of office, and the noble integrity of reclusion was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yet profit-seekers took the name of recluse to cheat their way into office, crowding the highways until Mount Zhongnan and the peaks of Song were nicknamed shortcuts to rank—and the high integrity of withdrawal was ruined.

sentences.zh: 故裒可喜慕者類於篇。

translations.literal: Therefore those gathered here who may be admired are classified in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Hence this chapter gathers only those whose lives are genuinely worthy of admiration.

sentences.zh: 王績，字無功，絳州龍門人。

translations.literal: Wang Ji, style name Wugong, was a man of Longmen in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji, courtesy name Wugong, was a native of Longmen in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 性簡放，不喜拜揖。

translations.literal: By nature simple and unrestrained, he disliked bowing and saluting.
translations.idiomatic: Unrestrained by nature, he disliked bows and formal salutes.

sentences.zh: 兄通，隋末大儒也，聚徒河、汾間，仿古作《六經》，又為《中說》以擬《論語》。

translations.literal: His elder brother Tong was a great Confucian of late Sui, gathering disciples between the Yellow and Fen rivers, imitating antiquity in composing the Six Classics and writing the Zhongshuo to parallel the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Wang Tong was a leading Confucian of late Sui, teaching between the Yellow and Fen rivers, composing imitations of the Six Classics and writing the Zhongshuo in the manner of the Analects.

sentences.zh: 不為諸儒稱道，故書不顯，惟《中說》獨傳。

translations.literal: The Confucians did not praise him, so his books did not become famous; only the Zhongshuo alone was transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Other scholars did not commend him, so most of his books went unknown; only the Zhongshuo survived.

sentences.zh: 通知績誕縱，不嬰以家事，鄉族慶吊冠昏，不與也。

translations.literal: Tong knew that Ji was wild from birth and did not burden him with household affairs; at village weddings, funerals, capping, and marriage he did not participate.
translations.idiomatic: Tong saw that Ji had been free-spirited from childhood and never pressed him into family duties; he skipped village weddings, funerals, cappings, and betrothals alike.

sentences.zh: 與李播、呂才善。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Li Bo and Lü Cai.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Li Bo and Lü Cai.

sentences.zh: 大業中，舉孝悌廉潔，授秘書省正字。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt and was appointed Rectifier in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign he was recommended as filial and incorrupt and appointed a rectifier in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 不樂在朝，求為六合丞，以嗜酒不任事，時天下亦亂，因劾，遂解去。

translations.literal: Unhappy at court, he asked to be magistrate of Liuhe; because of fondness for wine he could not perform his duties, and as the realm was also in disorder he was impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Unhappy in the capital, he asked for the post of magistrate of Liuhe; his love of wine left him unfit for duty, and with the empire falling into chaos he was impeached and removed.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「網羅在天，吾且安之！」

translations.literal: He sighed and said: "The net is in heaven—I shall rest beneath it!"
translations.idiomatic: He sighed, "Heaven's net is spread wide—I shall settle beneath it!

sentences.zh: 乃還鄉里。

translations.literal: Then he returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Then he went home.

sentences.zh: 有田十六頃在河渚間。

translations.literal: He had sixteen qing of fields on a river islet.
translations.idiomatic: He owned sixteen qing of fields on a river islet.

sentences.zh: 仲長子光者，亦隱者也，無妻子，結廬北渚，凡三十年，非其力不食。

translations.literal: Zhongchang Ziguang was also a recluse, without wife or children; he built a hut on the north islet and for thirty years ate only what his own labor provided.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchang Ziguang, another recluse, had neither wife nor children; he built a hut on the north islet and for thirty years ate only what he himself could earn.

sentences.zh: 績愛其真，徙與相近。

translations.literal: Ji loved his genuineness and moved to live near him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji admired his authenticity and moved nearby.

sentences.zh: 子光喑，未嘗交語，與對酌酒歡甚。

translations.literal: Ziguang was mute and never conversed; they only faced each other drinking wine with great delight.
translations.idiomatic: Ziguang was mute and never spoke; they simply drank together in silent joy.

sentences.zh: 績有奴婢數人，種黍，春秋釀酒，養鳧雁，蒔藥草自供。

translations.literal: Ji had several male and female servants who planted millet, brewed wine in spring and autumn, raised ducks and geese, and grew medicinal herbs for their needs.
translations.idiomatic: Ji kept several servants who planted millet, brewed wine each spring and autumn, raised ducks and geese, and grew herbs for the household.

sentences.zh: 以《周易》、《老子》、《莊子》置床頭，他書罕讀也。

translations.literal: He placed the Book of Changes, Laozi, and Zhuangzi at his bedside and rarely read other books.
translations.idiomatic: He kept the Book of Changes, the Laozi, and the Zhuangzi by his bed and seldom read anything else.

sentences.zh: 欲見兄弟，輒度河還家。

translations.literal: When he wished to see his brothers he would cross the river and return home.
translations.idiomatic: When he wished to see his brothers he crossed the river to visit them.

sentences.zh: 游北山東皋，著書自號東皋子。

translations.literal: Roaming the eastern slope of North Mountain, he wrote books and styled himself Master of the Eastern Slope.
translations.idiomatic: Wandering the eastern slope of North Mountain, he wrote and called himself Master of the Eastern Slope.

sentences.zh: 乘牛經酒肆，留或數日。

translations.literal: Riding an ox past wine shops, he would sometimes stay several days.
translations.idiomatic: Riding his ox past taverns, he sometimes lingered for days.

sentences.zh: 高祖武德初，以前官待詔門下省。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Gaozu's Wude reign he was retained at the Secretariat by his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Gaozu's Wude reign he was retained at court under his former office.

sentences.zh: 故事，官給酒日三升，或問：「待詔何樂邪？」

translations.literal: By precedent officials were given three sheng of wine a day; someone asked: "What pleasure is there in being a retained scholar?"
translations.idiomatic: By custom a retained scholar received three sheng of wine daily; someone asked, "What is pleasant about that post?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「良醞可戀耳！」

translations.literal: He answered: "Fine brew is worth lingering over!"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Only fine wine is worth the trouble!"

sentences.zh: 侍中陳叔達聞之，日給一斗，時稱「鬥酒學士」。

translations.literal: Attendant Chen Shuda heard this and gave him one dou a day; at the time he was called the "Scholar of a Dou of Wine."
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Chen Shuda heard of this and granted him a dou a day; people called him the Scholar of the Dou of Wine.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，以疾罷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was dismissed because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign illness forced him from office.

sentences.zh: 復調有司，時太樂署史焦革家善釀，績求為丞，吏部以非流不許，績固請曰：「有深意。」

translations.literal: He again petitioned the authorities; at that time the clerk of the Court of Imperial Music, Jiao Ge, brewed excellent wine, and Ji asked to be made his assistant; the Ministry of Personnel said he was not of the regular stream and refused, but Ji insisted: "There is a deep meaning in this."
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned again: Jiao Ge, a clerk in the Court of Imperial Music, brewed superb wine, and Ji asked to be made his deputy. Personnel refused because he was outside the regular career track, but Ji insisted, "There is a deeper reason.

sentences.zh: 竟除之。

translations.literal: In the end he was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he got the post.

sentences.zh: 革死，妻送酒不絕，歲餘，又死。

translations.literal: When Ge died his wife kept sending wine without cease; after more than a year she too died.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge died his wife continued the supply of wine; a year later she died as well.

sentences.zh: 績曰：「天不使我酣美酒邪？」

translations.literal: Ji said: "Does Heaven not wish me to drink good wine?"
translations.idiomatic: Ji cried, "Does Heaven mean to keep me from good wine?

sentences.zh: 棄官去。

translations.literal: He abandoned his post and left.
translations.idiomatic: He threw down his office and walked away.

sentences.zh: 自是太樂丞為清職。

translations.literal: From then on the post of assistant in the Court of Imperial Music became a pure office.
translations.idiomatic: After that the music-court deputyship was regarded as a pure and honorable post.

sentences.zh: 追述革酒法為經，又采杜康、儀狄以來善酒者為譜。

translations.literal: He traced Ge's brewing methods into a classic and collected worthy drinkers from Du Kang and Yidi onward into a genealogy.
translations.idiomatic: He set down Ge's brewing methods as a classic and compiled a genealogy of famous drinkers from Du Kang and Yidi onward.

sentences.zh: 李淳風曰：「君，酒家南、董也。」

translations.literal: Li Chunfeng said: "Sir, you are the Nan and Dong of the wine trade.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chunfeng said, "You are the wine world's answer to Dong Zhongshu and Nan Yue.

sentences.zh: 所居東南有磐石，立杜康祠祭之，尊為師，以革配。

translations.literal: Southeast of his dwelling was a boulder; he erected a shrine to Du Kang and honored him as master, with Ge as associate.
translations.idiomatic: A great stone lay southeast of his home; he built a shrine to Du Kang, honored him as master, and paired Ge beside him.

sentences.zh: 著《醉鄉記》以次劉伶《酒德頌》。

translations.literal: He wrote Record of the Land of Drunkenness to follow Liu Ling's Eulogy on the Virtue of Wine.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Record of the Land of Drunkenness as a companion piece to Liu Ling's Eulogy on the Virtue of Wine.

sentences.zh: 其飲至五斗不亂，人有以酒邀者，無貴賤輒往，著《五斗先生傳》。

translations.literal: He could drink five dou without disorder; whenever anyone invited him with wine, noble or base, he would go, and wrote Biography of the Five-Dou Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He could drink five dou without losing his wits; whoever invited him with wine, high or low, he would visit, and he wrote Biography of the Five-Dou Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 刺史崔喜悅之，請相見，答曰：「奈何坐召嚴君平邪？」

translations.literal: Prefect Cui Xi delighted in him and asked to meet; he answered: "How can one sit and summon Yan Junping?"
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Cui Xi admired him and asked for a meeting; he replied, "Would you summon Yan Junping to sit before you?

sentences.zh: 卒不詣。

translations.literal: In the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He never went.

sentences.zh: 杜之松，故人也，為刺史，請績講禮，答曰：「吾不能揖讓邦君門，談糟粕，棄醇醪也。」

translations.literal: Du Zhisong, an old acquaintance, became prefect and asked Ji to lecture on ritual; he answered: "I cannot bow and yield at a lord's gate or discuss dregs while abandoning fine wine."
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhisong, an old friend, became prefect and asked him to expound ritual; he answered, "I cannot bow at a magistrate's gate or talk of lees while spurning the vintage.

sentences.zh: 之松歲時贈以酒脯。

translations.literal: Zhisong each year at the seasons sent him wine and dried meat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhisong sent him wine and preserved meat every season.

sentences.zh: 初，兄凝為隋著作郎，撰《隋書》未成，死，績續餘功，亦不能成。

translations.literal: Earlier his brother Ning had been Sui Compiler of the National History and drafted the Book of Sui without finishing; when he died Ji continued the remaining work but also could not complete it.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Ning had been Sui compiler of the national history and left the Book of Sui unfinished at his death; Ji tried to finish it but could not.

sentences.zh: 豫知終日，命薄葬，自志其墓。

translations.literal: Foreknowing the day of his end, he ordered a plain burial and wrote his own tomb inscription.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the day of his death in advance, he ordered a plain burial and wrote his own epitaph.

sentences.zh: 績之仕，以醉失職，鄉人靳之，托無心子以見趣曰：「無心子居越，越王不知其大人也，拘之仕，無喜色。

translations.literal: Ji's losing office through drunkenness made his townspeople scorn him; he used the Heartless Child to show his intent, saying: "The Heartless Child lived in Yue; the king of Yue did not know he was a great man and detained him for office, yet he showed no joy.
translations.idiomatic: Because drink cost him his post, neighbors sneered at him; he told the tale of the Heartless Child: "The Heartless Child lived in Yue; the king did not know his worth and forced him into service, yet he showed no joy.

sentences.zh: 越國法曰：『穢行者不齒。』

translations.literal: Yue law said: 'One whose conduct is foul shall not be ranked among others.'
translations.idiomatic: Yue law declared, 'Whoever behaves foully shall not stand among decent men.

sentences.zh: 俄而無心子以穢行聞，王黜之，無慍色。

translations.literal: Soon the Heartless Child was known for foul conduct; the king dismissed him, yet he showed no anger.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Heartless Child was reported for foul conduct; the king dismissed him, yet he was not angry.

sentences.zh: 退而適茫蕩之野，過動之邑而見機士，機士撫髀曰：『嘻！

translations.literal: He withdrew to the vast wilds; passing the town of Motion he met a Clever Fellow, who slapped his thigh and said: 'Alas!
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to open country; in the town of Motion he met a Clever Fellow who slapped his thigh and cried, 'Alas!

sentences.zh: 子賢者而以罪廢邪？』

translations.literal: You are worthy yet cast out for a crime?
translations.idiomatic: You are worthy yet cast out for a crime?

sentences.zh: 無心子不應。

translations.literal: The Heartless Child did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The Heartless Child did not answer.

sentences.zh: 機士曰：『願見教。』

translations.literal: The Clever Fellow said: 'I wish to hear instruction.'
translations.idiomatic: The Clever Fellow said, 'I wish to learn from you.'

sentences.zh: 曰：『子聞蜚廉氏馬乎？

translations.literal: He said: 'Have you heard of Feilian's horses?
translations.idiomatic: He said, 'Have you heard of Feilian's horses?'

sentences.zh: 一者硃鬣白毳，龍骼鳳臆，驟馳如舞，終日不釋轡而以熱死；

translations.literal: One had vermilion mane and white fetlocks, dragon breast and phoenix barrel, galloping like a dance, never loosing the reins all day until it died of heat;
translations.idiomatic: One had a vermilion mane and white fetlocks, a dragon's chest and phoenix barrel, galloping like a dancer until, reins never slackened all day, it died of heat;

sentences.zh: 一者重頭昂尾，駝頸貉膝，啉是齧善蹶，棄諸野，終年而肥。

translations.literal: one had heavy head and raised tail, camel neck and badger knee, stumbling and biting, cast out to the wilds and growing fat all year.
translations.idiomatic: another had a heavy head and raised tail, camel neck and badger knee, stumbling and biting, turned loose in the wilds and growing fat all year.

sentences.zh: 夫鳳不憎山棲，龍不羞泥蟠，君子不苟潔以罹患，不避穢而養精也。』」

translations.literal: The phoenix does not disdain mountain roosting, the dragon is not ashamed to coil in mud; the gentleman does not fastidiously keep clean to invite calamity, nor avoid foulness to nourish his essence.'
translations.idiomatic: The phoenix does not scorn mountain perches, the dragon is not ashamed to coil in mud; the gentleman does not keep himself spotless to invite disaster, nor shuns foulness when it nourishes his spirit.

sentences.zh: 其自處如此。

translations.literal: Such was how he regarded himself.
translations.idiomatic: Such was how he thought of himself.

sentences.zh: 硃桃椎，益州成都人。

translations.literal: Zhu Taozhui was a man of Chengdu in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Taozhui was a native of Chengdu in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 澹泊絕俗，被裘曳索，人莫能測其為。

translations.literal: Tranquil and aloof from custom, wearing fur and dragging rope sandals, no one could fathom what he was.
translations.idiomatic: Serene and remote from the world, clad in fur and rope sandals, no one could tell what manner of man he was.

sentences.zh: 長史竇軌見之，遺以衣服、鹿幘、麂靴，逼署鄉正。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Dou Gui saw him and sent clothes, a deer-cap, and badger boots, forcing on him the post of village elder.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Dou Gui saw him and sent clothes, a deer-skin cap, and badger boots, pressing on him the post of village elder.

sentences.zh: 委之地，不肯服。

translations.literal: He threw them on the ground and would not wear them.
translations.idiomatic: He cast them on the ground and refused to wear them.

sentences.zh: 更結廬山中，夏則裸，冬緝木皮葉自蔽，贈遺無所受。

translations.literal: He built another hut in the mountains; in summer he went naked, in winter he stitched bark and leaves to cover himself, and would accept no gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He built another hut in the hills; in summer he went naked, in winter he stitched bark and leaves for cover, and accepted no gifts.

sentences.zh: 嘗織十芒屩置道上，見者曰：「居士屩也。」

translations.literal: He once wove ten straw sandals and set them on the road; passersby said: "These are the recluse's sandals.
translations.idiomatic: Once he wove ten straw sandals and left them on the road; passersby said, "Those are the recluse's sandals.

sentences.zh: 為鬻米茗易之，置其處，輒取去，終不與人接。

translations.literal: They sold rice and tea to exchange for them and left them in place; he always took them away and never dealt with people.
translations.idiomatic: People left rice and tea in exchange and he took the payment, but he never spoke with anyone.

sentences.zh: 其為屩，草柔細，環結促密，人爭躡之。

translations.literal: His sandals were of fine soft grass, tightly looped and dense; people competed to wear them.
translations.idiomatic: His sandals were woven of fine soft grass, tightly knotted; people vied to wear them.

sentences.zh: 高士廉為長史，備禮以請，降階與之語，不答，瞪視而出。

translations.literal: Gao Shilian was chief administrator and with full ritual invited him; descending the steps to speak with him, he did not answer but stared and walked out.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Shilian was chief administrator he invited him with full ceremony, came down the steps to speak, but Taozhui only stared and walked out.

sentences.zh: 士廉拜曰：「祭酒其使我以無事治蜀邪？」

translations.literal: Shilian bowed and said: "Has the libationer sent me to govern Shu without trouble?"
translations.idiomatic: Shilian bowed and said, "Has the libationer sent me to govern Shu in peace?

sentences.zh: 乃簡條目，薄賦斂，州大治。

translations.literal: Thereupon he simplified regulations and lightened taxes; the prefecture was greatly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: He then simplified laws and lightened levies, and the prefecture was well governed.

sentences.zh: 屢遣人存問，見輒走林草自匿云。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sent men to inquire after him; whenever seen he would flee into woods and grass to hide.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men again and again to inquire after Taozhui, who always fled into the thickets to hide.

sentences.zh: 孫思邈

translations.literal: Sun Simiao
translations.idiomatic: Sun Simiao

sentences.zh: 孫思邈，京兆華原人。

translations.literal: Sun Simiao was a man of Huayuan in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Simiao was a native of Huayuan in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 通百家說，善言老子、莊周。

translations.literal: He mastered the teachings of the hundred schools and was skilled in discoursing on Laozi and Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the teachings of the hundred schools and excelled at expounding Laozi and Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 周洛州總管獨孤信見其少，異之，曰：「聖童也，顧器大難為用爾！」

translations.literal: Dugu Xin, regional inspector of Zhou and Luo, saw him in youth and marveled, saying: "A holy child—yet his vessel is too great to be easily used!"
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Xin, inspector of Zhou and Luo, saw him young and exclaimed, "A sage child—but his talent is too great to be lightly employed!

sentences.zh: 及長，居太白山。

translations.literal: When grown he lived on Mount Taibai.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he lived on Mount Taibai.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝輔政，以國子博士召，不拜。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen assisted the government he was summoned as Erudite of the Directorate of Education but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen held the regency he was summoned as erudite of the Directorate of Education and declined.

sentences.zh: 密語人曰：「後五十年有聖人出，吾且助之。」

translations.literal: He said privately to others: "In fifty years a sage will appear; I shall assist him."
translations.idiomatic: He told others privately, "In fifty years a sage will arise; I mean to aid him.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，召詣京師，年已老，而聽視聰嘹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taizong he was summoned to the capital; though already old, his hearing and sight were keen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taizong's reign he was summoned to the capital; though aged, his hearing and sight were keen.

sentences.zh: 帝歎曰：「有道者！」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed: "A man of the Way!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed, "A man of the Way!

sentences.zh: 欲官之，不受。

translations.literal: He wished to give him office but he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to give him office, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，復召見，拜諫議大夫，固辭。

translations.literal: In the Xianqing era he was again summoned and made Remonstrating Grand Master but firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianqing era he was summoned again and offered the post of remonstrating grand master, but firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 上元元年，稱疾還山，高宗賜良馬，假鄱陽公主邑司以居之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan he pleaded illness and returned to the mountains; Gaozong bestowed fine horses and lent him the fief office of Princess Poyang to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangyuan 1 he pleaded illness and returned to the hills; Emperor Gaozong gave him fine horses and lent him the fief office of Princess Poyang for his residence.

sentences.zh: 思邈於陰陽、推步、醫藥無不善，孟詵、盧照鄰等師事之。

translations.literal: Simiao was without peer in yin-yang, calendrical calculation, and medicine; Meng Shen and Lu Zhaolin studied under him.
translations.idiomatic: Simiao had no equal in yin-yang lore, calendrical astronomy, or medicine; Meng Shen and Lu Zhaolin were among his disciples.

sentences.zh: 照鄰有惡疾，不可為，感而問曰：「高醫愈疾，奈何？」

translations.literal: Zhaolin had a grave illness beyond cure and asked in distress: "Great physicians cure illness—how is it done?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolin suffered an incurable illness and asked in anguish, "Great physicians heal disease—how?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「天有四時五行，寒暑迭居，和為雨，怒為風，凝為雨霜，張為虹霓，天常數也。

translations.literal: He answered: "Heaven has four seasons and five phases; cold and heat succeed each other; harmony becomes rain, anger becomes wind, congelation becomes frost and snow, expansion becomes rainbow—this is heaven's constant pattern.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Heaven has four seasons and five phases, cold and heat in turn; harmony becomes rain, anger wind, congelation frost and snow, expansion rainbows—that is heaven's constant way.

sentences.zh: 人之四支五藏，一覺一寐，吐納往來，流為榮衛，章為氣色，發為音聲，人常數也。

translations.literal: Man's four limbs and five viscera wake and sleep, exhale and inhale in circulation, flowing as nutritive and defensive qi, manifesting as complexion, issuing as voice—this is man's constant pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Man's four limbs and five viscera wake and sleep, breathe in and out, circulate nutritive and defensive qi, show color in the face and sound in the voice—that is man's constant way.

sentences.zh: 陽用其形，陰用其精，天人所同也。

translations.literal: Yang employs form, yin employs essence; heaven and man are alike in this.
translations.idiomatic: Yang uses form, yin uses essence; heaven and man share the same principle.

sentences.zh: 失則烝生熱，否生寒，結為瘤贅，陷為癰疽，奔則喘乏，端則燋槁，發乎面，動乎形。

translations.literal: When lost, steam generates heat, blockage generates cold, binding forms tumors and growths, sinking forms abscesses and boils, rushing brings panting exhaustion, extreme drying brings withering—issuing in the face, moving in the form.
translations.idiomatic: When the pattern is lost, congestion breeds heat and stagnation cold; knots become tumors, sinks become abscesses, rushing brings gasping exhaustion, extreme drying withers the flesh—first in the face, then in the limbs.

sentences.zh: 天地亦然：五緯縮贏，孛彗飛流，其危診也；

translations.literal: Heaven and earth are likewise: the five planets shrink and swell, comets fly—those are dangerous signs;
translations.idiomatic: So too with heaven and earth: the five planets wax and wane, comets streak—that is heaven's dangerous symptom;

sentences.zh: 寒暑不時，其蒸否也；

translations.literal: cold and heat untimely are its steam and blockage;
translations.idiomatic: untimely cold and heat are its congestion and stagnation;

sentences.zh: 石立土踴，是其瘤贅；

translations.literal: stones standing and earth swelling are its tumors and growths;
translations.idiomatic: stones thrusting up and earth swelling are its tumors;

sentences.zh: 山崩土陷，是其癰疽；

translations.literal: mountains collapsing and earth sinking are its abscesses and boils;
translations.idiomatic: mountains collapsing and earth sinking are its abscesses;

sentences.zh: 奔風暴雨其喘乏，川瀆竭涸其燋槁。

translations.literal: rushing wind and violent rain are its panting exhaustion, rivers and streams drying up are its withering.
translations.idiomatic: rushing storms are its gasping, rivers running dry its withering.

sentences.zh: 高醫導以藥石，救以钅乏劑；

translations.literal: Great physicians guide with drugs and stones and rescue with needle preparations;
translations.idiomatic: Great physicians guide with drugs and stone and rescue with needles and potions;

sentences.zh: 聖人和以至德，輔以人事。

translations.literal: sages harmonize with utmost virtue and assist with human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: sages harmonize through supreme virtue and assist through human effort.

sentences.zh: 故體有可愈之疾，天有可振之災。」

translations.literal: Therefore in the body there are illnesses that can be cured; in heaven there are disasters that can be remedied."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the body has illnesses that can be cured, and heaven has calamities that can be set right."

sentences.zh: 照鄰曰：「人事奈何？」

translations.literal: Zhaolin said: "What of human affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolin asked, "What of human affairs?

sentences.zh: 曰：「心為之君，君尚恭，故欲小。

translations.literal: [He] said: "The heart is their sovereign; a sovereign should be reverent, hence one should make it small.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Simiao replied: "The heart is the ruler of the body; because a ruler must be reverent, the heart should be kept small.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰『如臨深淵，如履薄冰』，小之謂也。

translations.literal: The Odes says, 'As if overlooking a deep abyss, as if treading on thin ice'—that is what is meant by small."
translations.idiomatic: As the Book of Odes has it—'as if facing a deep gulf, as if walking on thin ice'—that is the sense in which the heart should be small.

sentences.zh: 膽為之將，以果決為務，故欲大。

translations.literal: The gallbladder is their general; its task is firm resolve, hence one should make it large.
translations.idiomatic: The gallbladder is the body's commander-in-chief, charged with decisive action, and therefore should be made large.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰『赳赳武夫，公侯幹城』，大之謂也。

translations.literal: The Odes says, 'Stalwart is the warrior, bulwark of lords and marquises'—that is what is meant by large."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes' line 'bold and stalwart is the warrior, shield of duke and marquis' captures what is meant by large.

sentences.zh: 仁者靜，地之象，故欲方，《傳》曰『不為利回，不為義疚』，方之謂也。

translations.literal: The benevolent are still, like the image of earth, hence one should make them square; the Tradition says, 'Do not turn aside for profit, do not feel ashamed of righteousness'—that is what is meant by square.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence is stillness, the image of earth, and should be square; as the Zuozhuan puts it, 'not swayed by gain, not shamed by right conduct'—that is squareness.

sentences.zh: 智者動，天之象，故欲圓。

translations.literal: The wise are active, like the image of heaven, hence one should make them round.
translations.idiomatic: Wisdom is movement, the image of heaven, and should be kept round.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰『見機而作，不俟終日』，圓之謂也。」

translations.literal: The Changes says, 'When you see the moment, act; do not wait out the day'—that is what is meant by round."
translations.idiomatic: The Yijing counsels, 'See the turning point and act—do not wait for the day to end'; that is roundness."

sentences.zh: 復問養性之要，答曰：「天有盈虛，人有屯危，不自慎，不能濟也。

translations.literal: He again asked about the essentials of nurturing life, and [Simiao] answered: "Heaven has fullness and emptiness; people have hardship and peril—without self-caution, one cannot cross them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhaolin asked again about the essentials of nurturing life. Sun Simiao answered: "Heaven waxes and wanes; human lives meet crisis and danger. Without careful self-restraint, none of this can be weathered.

sentences.zh: 故養性必先知自慎也。

translations.literal: Therefore in nurturing life one must first know self-caution.
translations.idiomatic: To nurture life, one must first master cautious self-governance.

sentences.zh: 慎以畏為本，故士無畏則簡仁義，農無畏則墮稼穡，工無畏則慢規矩，商無畏則貸不殖，子無畏則忘孝，父無畏則廢慈，臣無畏則勳不立，君無畏則亂不治。

translations.literal: Caution takes reverent fear as its root; hence when scholars lack fear they slight benevolence and righteousness, when farmers lack fear they neglect the crops, when artisans lack fear they treat rules lightly, when merchants lack fear loans do not prosper, when sons lack fear they forget filial piety, when fathers lack fear they abandon kindness, when ministers lack fear meritorious service is not established, when rulers lack fear disorder is not governed.
translations.idiomatic: Caution is rooted in reverent awe. Without it, scholars neglect benevolence and righteousness, farmers abandon their fields, craftsmen scorn their gauges, merchants find credit unprofitable, sons forget filial duty, fathers set aside parental kindness, ministers win no lasting merit, and rulers cannot bring order from chaos.

sentences.zh: 是乙太上畏道，其次畏天，其次畏物，其次畏人，其次畏身。

translations.literal: Thus the highest reveres the Way, next reveres Heaven, next reveres things, next reveres people, next reveres the self.
translations.idiomatic: In order of rank: first revere the Way, then Heaven, then the things of the world, then other people, and finally one's own person.

sentences.zh: 憂于身者不拘於人，畏於己者不制於彼，慎於小者不懼於大，戒於近者不侮於遠。

translations.literal: Those who worry about the body are not constrained by others; those who fear themselves are not controlled by others; those cautious in small matters do not fear great ones; those on guard against what is near do not insult what is far.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever minds the body is not shackled by others; whoever stands in awe of himself is not mastered by the crowd; caution in small things dispels terror of the large; vigilance at hand keeps distant trouble at bay.

sentences.zh: 知此則人事畢矣。」

translations.literal: Knowing this, then human affairs are complete."
translations.idiomatic: Grasp this, and the conduct of human affairs is complete."

sentences.zh: 初，魏征等修齊、梁、周、隋等五家史，屢咨所遺，其傳最詳。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wei Zheng and others compiled the histories of Qi, Liang, Zhou, Sui, and the other five states, they repeatedly consulted him on what had been omitted; his entries are the most detailed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zheng and his colleagues compiled the histories of Qi, Liang, Zhou, Sui, and the other dynasties, they repeatedly sought Sun Simiao's counsel on lacunae in the record, and the passages bearing his name are among the fullest.

sentences.zh: 永淳初，卒，年百餘歲，遺令薄葬，不藏明器，祭去牲牢。

translations.literal: In the beginning of the Yongchun era he died, aged more than a hundred; his final instructions called for a plain burial, no grave goods stored, and sacrifices without sacrificial livestock.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Yongchun reign, aged over a hundred. He left orders for a spare funeral, no mingqi in the tomb, and offerings without slaughtered animals.

sentences.zh: 孫處約嘗以諸子見，思邈曰：「俊先顯，侑晚貴，佺禍在執兵。」

translations.literal: Sun Chuyue once brought his sons to see him; Simiao said: "Jun will rise first; You will attain rank late; Quan's calamity lies in bearing arms."
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Chuyue once presented his sons, Simiao said, "Jun will distinguish himself early, You will rise late, and Quan will meet disaster through military office.

sentences.zh: 後皆驗。

translations.literal: Afterwards all were verified.
translations.idiomatic: In every case his words proved true.

sentences.zh: 太子詹事盧齊卿之少也，思邈曰：「後五十年位方伯，吾孫為屬吏，願自愛。」

translations.literal: When Lu Qiqing was young, Chief Steward of the Heir Apparent, Simiao said: "Fifty years hence you will hold a regional command; my grandson will serve under you—take care of yourself."
translations.idiomatic: To the young Lu Qiqing, later Chief Steward of the Heir Apparent, Simiao foretold: "In fifty years you will be a regional inspector; my grandson will be your subordinate—mind how you treat him.

sentences.zh: 時思邈之孫溥尚未生，及溥為蕭丞，而齊卿徐州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time Simiao's grandson Pu had not yet been born; when Pu became magistrate of Xiao and Qiqing was prefect of Xuzhou, it came to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Pu had not yet been born; years later, when Pu served as magistrate of Xiao and Qiqing governed Xuzhou, the prophecy was fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 田遊岩

translations.literal: Tian Youyan
translations.idiomatic: Tian Youyan

sentences.zh: 田遊岩，京兆三原人。

translations.literal: Tian Youyan was a man of Sanyuan in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Youyan, a native of Sanyuan in the Jingzhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 永徽時，補太學生。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era he was appointed a student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui reign he entered the Imperial University as a student.

sentences.zh: 罷歸，入太白山。

translations.literal: He resigned and returned home, then went into Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: He left office, returned home, and withdrew to Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 母及妻皆有方外志，與共棲遲山水間。

translations.literal: His mother and wife both had aspirations beyond the world, and together they lingered among mountains and waters.
translations.idiomatic: His mother and wife shared his longing for life beyond the court, and the family settled together in mountain and stream country.

sentences.zh: 自蜀曆荊、楚，愛夷陵青溪，止廬其側。

translations.literal: From Shu he traveled through Jing and Chu, loved the Green Stream at Yiling, and built a hut on its bank.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling from Shu through Jing and Chu, he fell in love with the Green Stream at Yiling and built his dwelling on its banks.

sentences.zh: 長史李安期表其才，召赴京師，行及汝，辭疾入箕山，居許由祠旁，自號「由東鄰」，頻召不出。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Li Anqi memorialized his talent; he was summoned to the capital, but on reaching Ru he pleaded illness, entered Mount Ji, lived beside the shrine of Xu You, styled himself "Eastern Neighbor of [Xu] You," and though summoned repeatedly would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Li Anqi recommended him to court; he was summoned to the capital, but at Ru prefecture he pleaded illness, retired to Mount Ji beside Xu You's shrine, took the sobriquet "Xu You's Eastern Neighbor," and refused repeated imperial calls.

sentences.zh: 高宗幸嵩山，遣中書侍郎薛元超就問其母，賜藥物絮帛。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong visited Mount Song, he sent Vice Director of the Secretariat Xue Yuanchao to inquire after his mother and bestowed medicines, floss silk, and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: On Gaozong's tour of Mount Song, the emperor sent Vice Director of the Secretariat Xue Yuanchao to visit Youyan's mother with medicines, floss, and silk.

sentences.zh: 帝親至其門，遊岩野服出拜，儀止謹樸，帝令左右扶止，謂曰：「先生比佳否？」

translations.literal: The emperor came in person to his gate; Youyan came out in rustic dress to bow, his bearing plain and careful. The emperor had attendants support him and stop him, saying: "Sir, have you been well lately?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself came to his door. Youyan emerged in country clothes to pay his respects, every gesture restrained and plain. Gaozong had attendants steady him and asked, "Have you been well, sir?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「臣所謂泉石膏肓，煙霞痼疾者。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Your subject is what one calls a man with springs and stones in his marrow, mist and clouds a chronic ailment."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I am one of those whose marrow is springs and stone, whose chronic sickness is mist on the peaks."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕得君，何異漢獲四皓乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In gaining you, how is this unlike Han's winning the Four Whiteheads?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "To win you—is that not like the Han finding the Four Recluses of Mount Shang?"

sentences.zh: 薛元超贊帝曰：「漢欲廢嫡立庶，故四人者為出，豈如陛下親降岩穴邪？」

translations.literal: Xue Yuanchao praised the emperor, saying: "Han wished to depose the heir and establish a lesser son, hence those four men came forth—how can that compare with Your Majesty descending in person to the cliff dwelling?"
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yuanchao added, "The Four came out because the Han court meant to displace the heir—how can that compare with Your Majesty honoring a hermit in his own grotto?"

sentences.zh: 帝悅，因敕游岩將家屬乘傳赴都，拜崇文館學士。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and ordered Youyan to bring his household by post carriage to the capital and appointed him Scholar of the Chongwen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the emperor ordered Youyan's household brought to the capital by relay carriage and named him Scholar of the Chongwen Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 帝營奉天宮，遊岩舊宅直宮左，詔不聽毀。

translations.literal: When the emperor built Fengtian Palace, Youyan's former home stood directly to the palace's left; an edict forbade its destruction.
translations.idiomatic: When Fengtian Palace was built, his old house lay immediately to its left; an edict spared it from demolition.

sentences.zh: 天子自書榜其門，曰「隱士田游岩宅」。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven himself wrote the plaque for his gate: "Dwelling of the Recluse Tian Youyan."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor inscribed his gate himself: "Dwelling of the Recluse Tian Youyan."

sentences.zh: 進太子洗馬。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Groom of the Heir Apparent's Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Groom of the Heir Apparent's Chariot.

sentences.zh: 裴炎死，坐素厚善，放還山。

translations.literal: When Pei Yan was executed, [Youyan] was sent back to the mountains because he had long been on intimate terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: After Pei Yan's execution, Youyan was dismissed to the hills for his close friendship with him.

sentences.zh: 蠶衣耕食，不交當世，惟與韓法昭、宋之問為方外友云。

translations.literal: He wore coarse cloth and lived by the plow, had no dealings with the age, and only with Han Fazhao and Song Zhiwen was he a friend beyond the world.
translations.idiomatic: He dressed in homespun, farmed for his food, kept aloof from public life, and counted only Han Fazhao and Song Zhiwen among his companions in reclusion.

sentences.zh: 時又有史德義者，昆山人，居虎丘山。

translations.literal: At the time there was also Shi Deyi, a man of Kunshan, who lived on Tiger Hill.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time there was Shi Deyi of Kunshan, who lived on Tiger Hill.

sentences.zh: 騎牛帶瓢，出入廛野。

translations.literal: Riding an ox and carrying a gourd, he went in and out of market towns and fields.
translations.idiomatic: He rode an ox, carried a gourd, and wandered through towns and countryside.

sentences.zh: 高宗聞其名，召至洛陽，俄稱疾歸。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong heard his name and summoned him to Luoyang; before long he claimed illness and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong heard of him, summoned him to Luoyang, and soon afterward he pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 天授初，江南宣勞使周興薦之，復召赴都，擢朝散大夫。

translations.literal: In the beginning of the Tianshou era the Jiangnan merit-conferring commissioner Zhou Xing recommended him; he was again summoned to the capital and promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshou reign, Commissioner Zhou Xing recommended him; he was called again to court and made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 興死，免官歸，素譽頓衰。

translations.literal: When Xing died he was dismissed and returned home; his former reputation swiftly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Xing died, Deyi lost his office and went home, and his once-lofty name quickly faded.

sentences.zh: 孟詵，汝州梁人。

translations.literal: Meng Shen, a man of Liang in Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Shen, a native of Liang in Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，累遷鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and rose repeatedly to Fengge Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi degree carried him through repeated promotions to Attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 他日至劉禕之家，見賜金，曰：「此藥金也，燒之，火有五色氣。」

translations.literal: On another day he went to Liu Yizhi's house and saw bestowed gold; he said: "This is medicine gold; burn it and the flame will show five-colored vapor."
translations.idiomatic: Visiting Liu Yizhi's house another day, he saw imperial gold and said, "This is medicinal gold—burn it and five-colored vapors rise from the flame.

sentences.zh: 試之，驗。

translations.literal: They tried it and it was verified.
translations.idiomatic: They tested it, and so it proved.

sentences.zh: 武后聞，不悅，出為台州司馬，頻遷春官侍郎。

translations.literal: Empress Wu heard and was displeased; he was sent out as prefectural marshal of Taizhou and soon promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The empress took offense and banished him to Taizhou as prefectural marshal, though he was soon made Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 相王召為侍讀。

translations.literal: Prince Xiang summoned him as Reader-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiang of Dan summoned him as Reader-in-Attendance.

sentences.zh: 拜同州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，致仕，居伊陽山，治方藥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenlong era he retired from office, lived on Mount Yiyang, and compounded medicines.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shenlong reign he retired to Mount Yiyang and devoted himself to medical formulas.

sentences.zh: 睿宗召，將用之，以老固辭，賜物百段，詔河南春秋給羊酒糜粥。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong summoned him intending to employ him; he firmly declined on grounds of age and was given a hundred lengths of goods; an edict ordered Henan to supply mutton, wine, and gruel in spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong summoned him to serve at court; he pleaded old age and was refused, but received a hundred lengths of gifts and a standing order that Henan supply him mutton, wine, and gruel each spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 尹畢構以詵有古人風，名所居為子平里。

translations.literal: Prefect Bi Gou, because Shen had the air of the ancients, named his dwelling Ziping Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Bi Gou, finding in Shen the bearing of the ancients, named his residence Ziping Lane.

sentences.zh: 開元初，卒，年九十三。

translations.literal: In the beginning of the Kaiyuan era he died, aged ninety-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Kaiyuan reign, aged ninety-three.

sentences.zh: 詵居官頗刻斂，然以治稱。

translations.literal: In office Shen was rather exacting in levies, yet he was famed for his governance.
translations.idiomatic: As an official he could be severe in collection, yet he was praised for how he governed.

sentences.zh: 其閒居嘗語人曰：「養性者，善言不可離口，善藥不可離手。」

translations.literal: In retirement he once said to people: "For nurturing life, good words must not leave the mouth, good medicines must not leave the hand."
translations.idiomatic: In seclusion he once told others, "Who would nurture life must keep wholesome words on the lips and good medicine in the hand.

sentences.zh: 當時傳其當。

translations.literal: People of the time passed on his saying.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries made the line proverbial.

sentences.zh: 王友貞

translations.literal: Wang Youzhen
translations.idiomatic: Wang Youzhen

sentences.zh: 王友貞，懷州河內人。

translations.literal: Wang Youzhen was a man of Henei in Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Youzhen, a native of Henei in Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父知敬，善書隸。

translations.literal: His father Zhi Jing was skilled in clerical and standard script.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Zhijing excelled at clerical and standard script.

sentences.zh: 武后時，仕為麟台少監。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time he served as Vice Director of the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he served as Vice Director of the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 友貞少為司經局正字。

translations.literal: Youzhen in youth was a proofreader of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhen in his youth held the post of proofreader in the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 母病，醫言得人肉啖良已，友貞剔股以進，母疾愈。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill the physician said human flesh eaten would cure her well; Youzhen cut flesh from his thigh to present, and his mother's illness was cured.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, the doctor said only human flesh could cure her; Youzhen sliced flesh from his own thigh for her to eat, and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 詔旌表其門。

translations.literal: An edict honored his gate with a commemorative plaque.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered his gate honored with an official commendation.

sentences.zh: 素好學，訓誨子弟如嚴君。

translations.literal: He had always loved learning and instructed his sons and younger kin as a stern father would.
translations.idiomatic: A lifelong student, he taught sons and kin with a father's strict hand.

sentences.zh: 口不語人過，重然諾，時以為君子。

translations.literal: He never spoke of others' faults in his mouth, greatly valued keeping his word, and people of the time regarded him as a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He never gossiped of others' faults, held promises sacred, and his contemporaries called him a true gentleman.

sentences.zh: 曆長水令，罷歸。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Changshui, then resigned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Changshui, then retired home.

sentences.zh: 中宗在東宮，召為司儀郎，不就。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was Eastern Heir he summoned him as Master of Ceremonies, but he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was crown prince he was summoned as Master of Ceremonies; Youzhen declined to come.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，以太子中舍人征，固辭疾。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenlong era he was summoned as Attendant of the Heir Apparent's Household but firmly pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shenlong reign he was called as Attendant of the Heir Apparent's Household and again pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 詔致珍饌，給全祿終身，四時送其所，州縣存問。

translations.literal: An edict sent him delicacies and granted full salary for life; each season they were delivered to his place, and prefectures and counties were to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sent delicacies, granted him full salary for life with seasonal deliveries, and ordered local officials to call on him.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在東宮，表以蒲車召，不至。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong was Eastern Heir he memorialized to summon him in a rush-cart, but he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong was crown prince, a memorial summoned him in the ceremonial rush cart; he still would not come.

sentences.zh: 卒，年九十九，贈銀青光祿大夫，賴縣令弔祭。

translations.literal: He died aged ninety-nine; he was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Honor with Silver Seal, and the magistrate of Lai County performed the mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died at ninety-nine, was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Honor with Silver Seal, and the magistrate of Lai performed the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 王希夷

translations.literal: Wang Xiyi
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiyi

sentences.zh: 王希夷，徐州滕人。

translations.literal: Wang Xiyi was a man of Teng in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiyi, a native of Teng in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 家貧，父母喪，為人牧羊，取傭以葬。

translations.literal: His family was poor; when his parents died he herded sheep for others and took wages to bury them.
translations.idiomatic: Born poor, he herded sheep for hire to pay for his parents' burial when they died.

sentences.zh: 隱嵩山，師黃頤學養生四十年。

translations.literal: He hid on Mount Song and for forty years studied nurturing life under Huang Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to Mount Song and studied longevity arts under Huang Yi for forty years.

sentences.zh: 頤卒，更居兗州徂徠，與劉玄博友善。

translations.literal: When Yi died he moved on to live at Culai in Yanzhou and was friendly with Liu Xuanbo.
translations.idiomatic: After Huang Yi died he moved to Culai in Yanzhou and became close to Liu Xuanbo.

sentences.zh: 喜讀《周易》、《老子》，餌松柏葉、雜華，年七十餘，筋力柔強。

translations.literal: He delighted in reading the Changes and Laozi, took pine-and-cypress leaves and mixed flowers as food, and past seventy his sinews and strength were still supple.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the Yijing and Laozi, lived on pine needles and medicinal herbs, and past seventy remained lithe and strong.

sentences.zh: 刺史盧齊卿就謁問政，答曰：「『己所不欲，勿施於人』，此言足矣。」

translations.literal: Prefect Lu Qiqing came to call and asked about government; he answered: "'What you yourself do not desire, do not impose on others'—that saying is enough."
translations.idiomatic: When Prefect Lu Qiqing visited to ask about governing, he answered, "'Do not do to others what you would not wish done to you'—that single sentence is enough."

sentences.zh: 玄宗東巡狩，詔州縣敦勸見行在，時九十餘，帝令張說訪以政事，宦官扶入宮中，與語甚悅，拜國子博士，聽還山。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong made an eastern tour, he ordered prefectures and counties to urge [recluses] to appear at the imperial encampment; [Xiyi] was then over ninety. The emperor had Zhang Yue inquire of him on state affairs; eunuchs helped him into the palace. The emperor spoke with him at great length and was very pleased, appointed him Erudite of the Directorate of Education, and allowed him to return to the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: On Xuanzong's eastern tour, local officials were ordered to present recluses at the imperial camp; Xiyi was then past ninety. Zhang Yue was sent to sound him on policy; eunuchs helped him into the palace. The emperor conversed with him at length, delighted, named him Erudite of the Directorate of Education, and let him go home to the hills.

sentences.zh: 敕州縣春秋致束帛酒肉，仍賜絹百、衣一稱。

translations.literal: He ordered prefectures and counties to send bundles of silk, wine, and meat in spring and autumn, and moreover bestowed a hundred bolts of silk and one suit of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: An edict required prefectures to send silk, wine, and meat each spring and autumn, with a further gift of a hundred bolts of silk and a suit of robes.

sentences.zh: 李元愷

translations.literal: Li Yuankai
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuankai

sentences.zh: 李元愷，邢州人。

translations.literal: Li Yuankai was a man of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuankai, a native of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 博學，善天步律曆，性恭慎，未嘗敢語人。

translations.literal: Broadly learned, skilled in celestial pacing and calendrical astronomy, by nature reverent and cautious, he never dared speak to people [lightly].
translations.idiomatic: Widely learned, expert in astronomy and the calendar, he was by nature reverent and cautious and never spoke lightly with others.

sentences.zh: 宋璟嘗師之，既當國，厚遺以束帛，將薦之朝，拒不答。

translations.literal: Song Jing had once been his teacher; when Jing held the state, he sent a generous gift of silk and was about to recommend him to court, but [Yuankai] refused and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing had studied under him; once in power, Jing sent a rich gift of silk and meant to recommend him to court, but Yuankai would not accept or reply.

sentences.zh: 洺州刺史元行沖邀致之，問經義畢，贈衣服，辭曰：「吾軀不可服新麗，懼不稱以速咎也。」

translations.literal: Prefect of Luozhou Yuan Xingchong invited him; when the exposition of the classics was finished, Xingchong offered clothing, and he declined, saying: "My body cannot wear new finery—I fear it will not suit me and hasten misfortune."
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou Prefect Yuan Xingchong invited him; after their discussion of the classics, Xingchong offered robes. Yuankai declined: "This frame cannot wear fresh splendor—I fear the mismatch will bring swift calamity.

sentences.zh: 行沖垢衊復與之，不獲已而受。

translations.literal: Xingchong soiled them and offered them again; unable to refuse further, he accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Xingchong deliberately soiled the garments and offered them again; unable to refuse further, Yuankai took them.

sentences.zh: 俄報身所蠶素絲，曰：「義不受無妄財也。」

translations.literal: Before long he reported that the plain silk on his person was his own silkworms', saying: "On principle I do not accept unearned wealth."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he explained that the plain silk he wore came from his own silkworms: "I cannot in good conscience keep wealth I did not earn.

sentences.zh: 先是，定州崔元鑒善《禮》學，用張易之力，授朝散大夫，家居給半祿。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cui Yuanjian of Dingzhou was skilled in ritual learning; through Zhang Yizhi's influence he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and at home was granted half salary.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cui Yuanjian of Dingzhou, learned in ritual, had used Zhang Yizhi's patronage to win the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and half pay while living at home.

sentences.zh: 元愷誚曰：「無功而祿，災也。」

translations.literal: Yuankai mocked him, saying: "Salary without merit is disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Yuankai mocked him: "Stipend without merit is its own disaster.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十餘。

translations.literal: He died aged over eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his eighties.

sentences.zh: 衛大經

translations.literal: Wei Dajing
translations.idiomatic: Wei Dajing

sentences.zh: 衛大經，蒲州解人。

translations.literal: Wei Dajing was a man of Jie in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Dajing, a native of Jie in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 卓然高行，口無二言。

translations.literal: Towering in conduct, in his mouth there was never a second word.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and austere in conduct, he never spoke an idle or contradictory word.

sentences.zh: 武后時，召之，固辭疾。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time he was summoned but firmly pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he was summoned to court and firmly pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 素善魏夏侯乾童，聞其母卒，盛暑步往吊，或止之曰：「方夏，涉遠不如致書。」

translations.literal: He had long been on good terms with Xiahou Qiantong of Weizhou; hearing that Qiantong's mother had died, in the height of summer he walked to offer condolences. Some tried to stop him, saying: "It is midsummer—going so far on foot is not as good as sending a letter."
translations.idiomatic: He had long been intimate with Xiahou Qiantong of Weizhou; learning that Qiantong's mother had died, he walked through the midsummer heat to mourn. Some urged him to stay: "In this heat, a letter would serve as well as such a journey.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「書能盡意邪？」

translations.literal: He answered: "Can a letter exhaust one's intent?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Can ink on paper exhaust what the heart must say?"

sentences.zh: 比至，乾童以事行，乃設席行吊禮，不訊其家而還。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Qiantong was away on business; he therefore set out mats and performed the mourning rites, did not inquire of the household, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Qiantong was away on business; Dajing spread mats at the door, performed the mourning rites, asked nothing of the family, and went home.

sentences.zh: 開元初，畢構為刺史，使縣令孔慎言就謁，辭不見。

translations.literal: In the beginning of the Kaiyuan era, when Bi Gou was prefect, he had Magistrate Kong Shenyan go to call on him; he declined and would not be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan, when Bi Gou was prefect, he sent Magistrate Kong Shenyan to call; Dajing refused to receive him.

sentences.zh: 大經邃于《易》，人謂之「《易》聖」。

translations.literal: Dajing was profound in the Changes; people called him "Sage of the Changes."
translations.idiomatic: Deep in the Yijing, contemporaries called him the Sage of the Changes.

sentences.zh: 豫筮死日，鑿墓自為志，如言終。

translations.literal: He divined in advance the day of his death, dug his tomb, and composed his own epitaph; he ended as foretold.
translations.idiomatic: He divined the day of his death in advance, dug his own grave, wrote his epitaph, and died exactly as he had foretold.

sentences.zh: 武攸緒

translations.literal: Wu Youxu
translations.idiomatic: Wu Youxu

sentences.zh: 武攸緒，則天皇后兄惟良子也。

translations.literal: Wu Youxu was a son of Empress Wu Zetian's elder brother Youliang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Youxu was the son of Youliang, elder brother to Empress Wu Zetian.

sentences.zh: 恬淡寡欲，好《易》、莊周書。

translations.literal: Tranquil and with few desires, he loved the Book of Changes and the writings of Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Even-tempered and sparing in his wants, he delighted in the Book of Changes and the works of Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 少變姓名，賣卜長安市，得錢輒委去。

translations.literal: In youth he changed his name, practiced divination in Chang'an market, and whenever he got money would cast it away.
translations.idiomatic: While young he assumed another name, told fortunes in the markets of Chang'an, and cast aside whatever coins he earned.

sentences.zh: 後更授太子通事舍人，累遷揚州大都督府長史、鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: Later he was again appointed Attendant Gentleman for Palace Communications to the Heir Apparent, and rose through posts to Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Prefecture and Vice Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned to office as Attendant Gentleman for Palace Communications to the Heir Apparent, then advanced to chief administrator of the Yangzhou metropolitan prefecture and vice minister of ceremonial affairs.

sentences.zh: 後革命，封安平郡王，從封中嶽，固辭官，願隱居。

translations.literal: After the dynastic revolution he was enfeoffed as Prince of Anping, followed the fengshan at the central peak, firmly declined office, and wished to live in seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Zetian overturned the Tang and founded her Zhou, he was enfeoffed Prince of Anping; he accompanied the court to Mount Song for the fengshan rites, yet steadfastly refused rank and asked to withdraw from public life.

sentences.zh: 後疑其詐，許之，以觀所為。

translations.literal: The Empress later suspected this was pretense, granted it, and watched what he would do.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress at first suspected he was feigning, but allowed his request so she could see how he behaved.

sentences.zh: 攸緒廬岩下如素遁者，後遣其兄攸宜敦諭，卒不起，後乃異之。

translations.literal: Youxu built a hut beneath the cliffs like one long in hiding; later she sent his elder brother Youyi to urge him earnestly, yet in the end he would not rise, and only then did she regard him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Youxu lived in a thatched shelter on the cliffs as though he had long been a recluse. The Empress then sent his brother Youyi to press him, but he still would not take office; at last she marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 盤桓龍門、少室間，冬蔽茅椒，夏居石室，所賜金銀鐺鬲、野服，王公所遺鹿裘、素障、癭杯，塵皆流積，不禦也。

translations.literal: He wandered between Longmen and Mount Song; in winter he sheltered under thatch and brush, in summer he dwelt in stone chambers. Gold and silver cauldrons and tripods bestowed on him, rustic garments, deer-fur robes, plain screens, and burl-wood cups sent by kings and dukes—all lay heaped with flowing dust, for he would not brush them away.
translations.idiomatic: Roaming between Longmen and Mount Song, he wintered beneath thatch and brush and summered in stone cells. Imperial gifts of gold and silver vessels, his own coarse dress, and deer-hide robes, plain screens, and gnarled cups from nobles all gathered dust in piles, for he never troubled to clean them.

sentences.zh: 市田潁陽，使家奴雜作，自混於民。

translations.literal: He bought fields at Yingyang and had household slaves labor among the common folk, mingling himself with the people.
translations.idiomatic: He purchased farmland at Yingyang and set his household slaves to work alongside commoners, blending himself into the crowd.

sentences.zh: 晚年肌肉消眚，瞳有紫光，晝能見星。

translations.literal: In his later years his flesh wasted away, his pupils held a purple light, and by day he could see the stars.
translations.idiomatic: In old age his body thinned to skin and bone, his pupils shone with a violet gleam, and he could discern stars even in daylight.

sentences.zh: 中宗初，降封巢國公，遣國子司業杜慎盈齎書以安車召，拜太子賓客。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhongzong's reign his rank was lowered to Duke of Chao; Du Shenying, Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, was sent with a letter to summon him in a honor carriage, and he was appointed Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong first took the throne, Youxu's title was reduced to Duke of Chao. Du Shenying, vice director of the Directorate of Education, was dispatched with an imperial letter to summon him in a state carriage, and he was appointed grand mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 苦祈還山，詔可。

translations.literal: He earnestly begged to return to the mountains; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded bitterly to go back to the hills, and the throne granted his request.

sentences.zh: 安樂公主出降，又遣通事舍人李邈以璽書迎之。

translations.literal: When Princess Anle married, the emperor again sent the Attendant Gentleman for Palace Communications Li Miao with a seal-letter to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Anle wed, the emperor once more sent Attendant Gentleman Li Miao with an imperial missive to bring him to court.

sentences.zh: 將至，帝敕有司即兩儀殿設位，行問道禮，詔見日山帔葛巾，不名不拜。

translations.literal: As he was about to arrive, the emperor ordered the relevant offices to set a place in the Hall of Two Principles and perform the ceremony of inquiring about the Way, decreeing that on the day of audience he should wear a mountain stole and hemp cap, and neither be named nor bow.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, the emperor commanded that a seat be prepared in the Hall of Two Principles for the rite of inquiring into the Way, and decreed that on the day of audience he should wear a hermit's stole and hemp cap, without being named or required to bow.

sentences.zh: 攸緒至，更冠帶。

translations.literal: When Youxu arrived, he again donned cap and belt.
translations.idiomatic: When Youxu came, he put on official cap and sash once more.

sentences.zh: 仗入，通事舍人贊就位，攸緒趨就常班再拜，帝愕然，禮不及行，朝廷歎息。

translations.literal: He entered leaning on a staff; the Attendant Gentleman for Palace Communications announced his taking position, and Youxu hurried to the regular court ranks and bowed twice. The emperor was startled; the rite could not be carried through, and the court sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Leaning on a staff he entered. As the attendant announced him to his place, Youxu hastened instead to the ordinary court rows and bowed twice. The emperor was dumbfounded; the intended ceremony never took place, and the whole court sighed.

sentences.zh: 賜予無所受，親貴來謁，道寒溫外，默無所言。

translations.literal: He accepted none of the gifts offered; when kin and the eminent came to call, beyond remarks on cold and heat he remained silent.
translations.idiomatic: He refused every gift pressed on him. When relatives and grandees visited, beyond a word on the weather he would say nothing.

sentences.zh: 及還，中書、門下、學士、朝官五品以上，並祖城東。

translations.literal: On his return, officials of the Secretariat and Chancellery, academicians, and court officials of the fifth rank and above all saw him off at the east gate of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When he left, secretariat and chancellery officials, Hanlin scholars, and every courtier of fifth rank or higher escorted him to the city's eastern gate.

sentences.zh: 俄而諸韋誅，武氏連禍，唯攸緒不及。

translations.literal: Before long the faction of Wei was executed; the Wu clan suffered disaster together, and only Youxu was untouched.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Wei faction was purged and the Wu kindred swept into ruin; Youxu alone escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 睿宗恐其不自安，下詔慰諭，復召拜太子賓客，不就。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong, fearing he might not feel secure, issued an edict of reassurance and again summoned him as Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong, anxious lest he feel unsafe, sent a comforting edict and summoned him once more as grand mentor to the heir apparent, but he would not take the post.

sentences.zh: 譙王重福之亂，攸緒以誣被系，張說表置廬山，中書令姚元崇奏：「攸緒在武后時未嘗輒出，今州縣逼遣，士為驚嗟。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Prince of Qiao Chongfu, Youxu was imprisoned on false charges; Zhang Yue memorialized that he be placed at Mount Lu, and Chief Minister Yao Yuanchong submitted: 'In Empress Wu's time Youxu never lightly came forth; now the prefectures and counties force him to go, and scholars are shocked and lament.
translations.idiomatic: During the rebellion of Prince Chongfu of Qiao, Youxu was jailed on trumped-up charges. Zhang Yue memorialized to lodge him on Mount Lu, and Chief Minister Yao Yuanchong wrote: 'Under Empress Wu, Youxu would not stir from seclusion; now local officials hound him to travel, to the astonishment and grief of the learned.

sentences.zh: 願詔賜嵩山舊居，令州縣存問。」

translations.literal: I beg that an edict grant his old dwelling on Mount Song and order the prefectures and counties to inquire after his welfare.'
translations.idiomatic: I ask that he be granted his former home on Mount Song and that prefectural officials be charged to look after him.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 開元十一年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the eleventh year of Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kaiyuan 11 (723).

sentences.zh: 白履忠

translations.literal: Bai Lüzhong
translations.idiomatic: Bai Lüzhong

sentences.zh: 白履忠，汴州浚儀人。

translations.literal: Bai Lüzhong was a man of Junyi in Bian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Lüzhong came from Junyi in Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 貫知文史，居古大梁城，時號梁丘子。

translations.literal: Thoroughly versed in literature and history, he lived in the ancient city of Daliang, and at the time was called Master Liangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply learned in letters and history, he made his home in the ancient city of Daliang and was known in his day as Master Liangqiu.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，召為校書郎，棄官去。

translations.literal: In the Jingyun era he was summoned as collator, but abandoned office and left.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyun period he was called up as a collating editor, then threw down his post and walked away.

sentences.zh: 開元十年，刑部尚書王志愔薦履忠博學守操，可代褚無量、馬懷素入閣侍讀，國子祭酒楊瑒又表其賢，召赴京師。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan, Minister of Justice Wang Zhiyin recommended Lüzhong as learned and steadfast in conduct, fit to replace Chu Wuliang and Ma Huaiyi in attending the emperor for study within the palace, and the Director of the Directorate of Education Yang Cheng also memorialized his worth; he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 10 (722), Minister of Justice Wang Zhiyin urged that Lüzhong's erudition and integrity suited him to succeed Chu Wuliang and Ma Huaiyi as a palace reader, and the director of education Yang Cheng also praised him; he was summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 辭病老不任職，詔拜朝散大夫。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and old age, unfit for office; an edict appointed him Grand Master of Palace Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded age and infirmity, unfit to serve; the court named him Grand Master of Palace Leisure.

sentences.zh: 乞還，手詔許游京師，徐返里閭。

translations.literal: He begged to return; by handwritten edict he was permitted to linger in the capital and then slowly go back to his native lanes.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to go home; the emperor's own brush granted him time to stroll the capital before drifting back to his village.

sentences.zh: 履忠留數月乃去。

translations.literal: Lüzhong stayed several months and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Lüzhong remained a few months more and then left.

sentences.zh: 吳兢，其里人也，謂曰：「子素貧，不沾斗米匹帛，雖得五品亦何益？」

translations.literal: Wu Jing, a fellow townsman, said to him: 'You have always been poor and never touched a peck of grain or a bolt of silk—even if you gain the fifth rank, what good is it?
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jing, a man of his home district, told him: 'You have always been poor and never touched official grain or silk. Even a fifth-rank title—what would it add?

sentences.zh: 履忠曰：「往契丹入寇，家取排門夫，吾以讀書，縣為免。

translations.literal: Lüzhong said: 'When the Khitans raided in the past, the district took men for gate guards; because I read books, the county exempted me.
translations.idiomatic: Lüzhong replied: 'When the Khitans invaded, the district drafted gate guards from every household. Because I was a reader of books, the county excused me.

sentences.zh: 今終身高臥，寬徭役，豈易得哉！」

translations.literal: Now to lie abed the rest of my life and enjoy lighter corvée—how easily could that be had!'
translations.idiomatic: Now I may rest out my days with lighter labor service. That is no small thing to come by!'

sentences.zh: 盧鴻，字顥然，其先幽州范陽人，徙洛陽。

translations.literal: Lu Hong, styled Haoran; his ancestors were men of Fanyang in You prefecture, and the family moved to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hong, courtesy name Haoran, was descended from families of Fanyang in Youzhou who had relocated to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 博學，善書籀。

translations.literal: Broadly learned, skilled in seal and clerical scripts.
translations.idiomatic: He was widely read and accomplished in seal and clerical calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 廬嵩山。

translations.literal: He built his hut on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: He made his dwelling on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元初，備禮征再，不至。

translations.literal: In the early Kaiyuan of Emperor Xuanzong he was summoned with full rites twice, but did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xuanzong's Kaiyuan reign he was twice summoned with full court ceremony, and twice he stayed away.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔曰：「鴻有泰一之道，中庸之德，鉤深詣微，確乎自高。

translations.literal: In the fifth year an edict said: 'Hong possesses the Way of the Grand Unity and the virtue of the Mean; probing the deep and reaching the subtle, he is firmly lofty in himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year an edict declared: 'Hong holds the Way of the Grand Unity and the virtue of equilibrium; plumbing depths and subtle truths, he stands aloof and self-possessed.

sentences.zh: 詔書屢下，每輒辭托，使朕虛心引領，於今數年。

translations.literal: Imperial letters have descended again and again, and each time he declines and makes excuses, so that We have led Our mind forth in vain for these several years.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial summons have gone out again and again, and each time he declines with excuses, leaving Us to strain forward in vain these many years.

sentences.zh: 雖得素履幽人之介，而失考父滋恭之誼，豈朝廷之故與生殊趣邪？

translations.literal: Though one gains the integrity of a man of the wilds, one loses the ever-deepening reverence of Kaofu—is it that court and recluse are of utterly different bent?
translations.idiomatic: He keeps the integrity of a mountain hermit, yet lacks the ever-deepening deference of Kaofu. Are court and hillside truly worlds apart?

sentences.zh: 將縱欲山林，往而不能返乎？

translations.literal: Will he indulge his desires in hills and forests, go, and never return?
translations.idiomatic: Or will he indulge the hills and forests, wander off, and never turn back?

sentences.zh: 禮有大倫，君臣之義不可廢也。

translations.literal: Rites have their great bonds; the meaning of ruler and minister cannot be cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual has its great bonds; the relation of ruler and minister cannot be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 今城闕密邇，不足為勞，有司其齎束帛之具，重宣茲旨，想有以翻然易節，副朕意焉。」

translations.literal: Now the capital is close at hand and should not be burdensome; let the relevant offices carry silks and gifts, proclaim this intent anew, and We trust he will turn his heart and change his course, fulfilling Our wish.'
translations.idiomatic: The capital is near and should not weary him. Let the proper offices bear silks and gifts and proclaim this anew. We trust he will turn his heart, change his course, and answer Our wish.'

sentences.zh: 鴻至東都，謁見不拜，宰相遣通事舍人問狀，答曰：「禮者，忠信所薄，臣敢以忠信見。」

translations.literal: Hong reached the eastern capital; on audience he did not bow. The chief minister sent the Attendant Gentleman for Palace Communications to question him; he answered: 'Rites are what loyalty and faith adhere to—I dare present myself through loyalty and faith.'
translations.idiomatic: Hong came to the eastern capital and on audience did not bow. The chief minister sent an attendant to question him; he replied: 'Rites are where loyalty and sincerity attach—I dare meet you through loyalty and sincerity alone.

sentences.zh: 帝召升內殿，置酒。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him to the inner hall and set out wine.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called him into the inner hall and offered wine.

sentences.zh: 拜諫議大夫，固辭。

translations.literal: He was appointed Remonstrating Grand Master, but firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Remonstrating Grand Master, but steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 復下制，許還山，歲給米百斛、絹五十，府縣為致其家，朝廷得失，其以狀聞。

translations.literal: An edict was again issued permitting him to return to the mountains, with a yearly grant of a hundred hu of grain and fifty bolts of silk; the prefecture and county were to deliver them to his home, and he was to report the gains and losses of the court as he saw them.
translations.idiomatic: A second decree allowed him back to the mountains with an annual stipend of a hundred hu of grain and fifty bolts of silk, delivered by local officials to his door, and he was to report what he observed of the court's right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 將行，賜隱居服，官營草堂，恩禮殊渥。

translations.literal: As he was about to go, he was given hermit's garb; the government built his thatched hall, and the favor was exceptionally generous.
translations.idiomatic: On his departure he received a recluse's robe; the state built his mountain lodge, and the honors were unusually lavish.

sentences.zh: 鴻到山中，廣學廬，聚徒至五百人。

translations.literal: Hong reached the mountains, broadened his study halls, and gathered disciples until they reached five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Back on Mount Song he enlarged his lecture halls until five hundred disciples gathered about him.

sentences.zh: 及卒，帝賜萬錢。

translations.literal: When he died, the emperor bestowed ten thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the emperor granted ten thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 鴻所居室，自號寧極云。

translations.literal: The dwelling in which Hong lived he himself styled Tranquil Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: He called the place where he lived Tranquil Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 吳筠，字貞節，華州華陰人。

translations.literal: Wu Yun, styled Zhenjie, was a man of Huayin in Hua prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yun, courtesy name Zhenjie, came from Huayin in Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 通經誼，美文辭，舉進士不中。

translations.literal: He mastered the classics and their meaning, excelled in literary composition, and took the Presented Scholar examination without success.
