translations.idiomatic: He mastered the classics and their glosses, wrote elegant prose, and failed the presented-scholar examination.

sentences.zh: 性高鯁，不耐沈浮于時，去居南陽倚帝山。

translations.literal: By nature lofty and unyielding, unable to endure the world's ups and downs, he left and dwelt on Mount Yidi in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Proud and unbending by nature, he could not bear the world's rise and fall, so he withdrew to Mount Yidi in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，召至京師，請隸道士籍，乃入嵩山依潘師正，究其術。

translations.literal: In the early Tianbao era he was summoned to the capital; he asked to be entered on the register of Daoist priests, then entered Mount Song to study under Pan Shizheng and exhaust his arts.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao reign he was called to the capital, petitioned to be registered as a Daoist priest, entered Mount Song under Pan Shizheng, and pursued the arts to their depth.

sentences.zh: 南遊天臺，觀滄海，與有名士相娛樂，文辭傳京師。

translations.literal: He traveled south to Tiantai, gazed on the blue sea, and enjoyed himself with famous gentlemen; his writings spread through the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He wandered south to Tiantai, looked out on the eastern sea, and kept company with celebrated men; his writings soon filled the capital.

sentences.zh: 玄宗遣使召見大同殿，與語甚悅，敕待詔翰林，獻《玄綱》三篇。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong sent envoys to summon him to audience in the Hall of Great Unity; speaking with him, he was greatly pleased, ordered him to await edicts in the Hanlin, and Yun presented three chapters of the Dark Net.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong summoned him to the Hall of Great Unity, delighted in their talk, made him a Hanlin attendant awaiting edicts, and received his three chapters of the Dark Net.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問道，對曰：「深於道者，無如《老子》五千文，其餘徒喪紙劄耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor once asked about the Way; he answered: 'For depth in the Way there is nothing like the five thousand words of Laozi; the rest are merely wasted paper.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked about the Way, he answered: 'Nothing goes deeper than the five thousand words of Laozi; everything else is wasted paper.

sentences.zh: 復問神仙治煉法，對曰：「此野人事，積歲月求之，非人主宜留意。」

translations.literal: He was again asked about the methods of immortals and alchemical refining; he answered: 'These are affairs of men in the wilds, pursued through accumulated years—not what a ruler should heed.'
translations.idiomatic: Asked about immortality and elixir refining, he said: 'Those are pursuits of mountain dwellers, labored over for years—not what a Son of Heaven should mind.'

sentences.zh: 筠每開陳，皆名教世務，以微言諷天子，天子重之。

translations.literal: Whenever Yun spoke forth, it was on famous teachings and the affairs of the age; with subtle words he admonished the Son of Heaven, and the Son of Heaven held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke, it was of moral teaching and the business of the realm; in delicate phrases he admonished the throne, and the throne weighed him heavily.

sentences.zh: 群沙門嫉其見遇，而高力士素事浮屠，共短筠於帝，筠亦知天下將亂，懇求還嵩山。

translations.literal: The Buddhist monks as a group resented his favored treatment; Gao Lishi had long served the Buddha, and together they slandered Yun to the emperor. Yun also knew the realm would soon fall into chaos, and earnestly begged to return to Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist clergy envied his favor at court; Gao Lishi, a lifelong patron of Buddhism, joined them in speaking ill of him to the emperor. Yun, sensing chaos ahead, pleaded earnestly to return to Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 詔為立道館。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a Daoist abbey built for him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commanded that a Daoist abbey be built for him.

sentences.zh: 安祿山欲稱兵，乃還茅山。

translations.literal: When An Lushan was about to raise troops, he returned to Mount Mao.
translations.idiomatic: As An Lushan prepared to rebel, he went back to Mount Mao.

sentences.zh: 而兩京陷，江、淮盜賊起，因東入會稽剡中。

translations.literal: When the two capitals fell and bandits rose on the Yangzi and Huai, he went east into Kuaiji and the Shan valleys.
translations.idiomatic: After both capitals fell and brigands swarmed the Yangzi and Huai, he traveled east into Kuaiji and the Shan stream country.

sentences.zh: 大曆十三年卒，弟子私諡為宗元先生。

translations.literal: He died in the thirteenth year of Dali; his disciples privately gave him the posthumous title Master Zongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Dali 13 (778); his disciples privately styled him Master Zongyuan.

sentences.zh: 始，蟋嘻惡於力士而斥，故文章深詆釋氏。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Jun bore a grudge against Lishi for having censured him, and therefore in his writings he deeply reviled the Buddhist church.
translations.idiomatic: At first, because Gao Lishi had rebuked him, Yun resented him and filled his writings with fierce attacks on Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 筠所善孔巢父、李白，歌詩略相甲乙云。

translations.literal: Those Yun favored—Kong Chaofu and Li Bai—their songs and poems were roughly on a par, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chaofu and Li Bai, whom Yun befriended, were said to match him poem for poem.

sentences.zh: 潘師正

translations.literal: Pan Shizheng
translations.idiomatic: Pan Shizheng

sentences.zh: 潘師正者，貝州宗城人。

translations.literal: Pan Shizheng was a man of Zongcheng in Bei prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Shizheng came from Zongcheng in Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 少喪母，廬墓，以孝聞。

translations.literal: He lost his mother while young, built a hut at her tomb, and was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died when he was young; he kept vigil at her tomb and won renown for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 事王遠知為道士，得其術，居逍遙穀。

translations.literal: He studied under Wang Yuanzhi as a Daoist priest, obtained his arts, and dwelt in Roaming Vale.
translations.idiomatic: He became a Daoist disciple of Wang Yuanzhi, mastered his techniques, and lived in Roaming Vale.

sentences.zh: 高宗幸東都，召見，問所須，對曰：「茂松清泉，臣所須也，既不乏矣。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong visited the eastern capital he summoned and saw him, asking what he required; he answered: 'Luxuriant pines and clear springs are what your subject needs, and of those he lacks nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong came to the eastern capital he summoned him and asked what he wished for; he replied: 'Your subject needs only lofty pines and clear springs, and those he already has in plenty.

sentences.zh: 帝尊異之，詔即其廬作崇唐觀。

translations.literal: The emperor honored him exceptionally and ordered a Chongtang Abbey built at his hut.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated him with special distinction and ordered Chongtang Abbey erected at his dwelling.

sentences.zh: 及營奉天宮，又敕直逍遙穀作門曰仙遊，北曰尋真。

translations.literal: When the Fengtian Palace was being built, he was again ordered to mark gates at Roaming Vale—south called Seeking the Immortals, north called Seeking the True.
translations.idiomatic: While the Fengtian Palace was under construction, he was again commanded to name gates at Roaming Vale: to the south, Seeking Immortals; to the north, Seeking Truth.

sentences.zh: 時太常獻新樂，帝更名《祈仙》、《望仙》、《翹仙曲》。

translations.literal: When the Court of Imperial Sacrifices presented new music, the emperor renamed the pieces Praying to Immortals, Gazing at Immortals, and Rising toward Immortals.
translations.idiomatic: When the Court of Imperial Sacrifices offered new music, the emperor retitled the pieces Praying to Immortals, Gazing at Immortals, and Soaring toward Immortals.

sentences.zh: 卒，年九十八，贈太中大夫，諡體玄先生。

translations.literal: He died at ninety-eight; posthumously he was given Grand Master of the Palace and the posthumous title Master Tixuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died at ninety-eight, and was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Palace with the posthumous title Master Tixuan.

sentences.zh: 又有劉道合者，亦與師正同居嵩山，帝即所隱立太一觀，使居之。

translations.literal: There was also Liu Daohe, who likewise lived on Mount Song with Shizheng; the emperor built the Taiyi Abbey at his place of seclusion and had him dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Liu Daohe, who shared Mount Song with Shizheng; the emperor founded Taiyi Abbey at his retreat and installed him there.

sentences.zh: 時將封太山，雨不止，帝令道合禳祝，俄而霽，乃令馳傳先行太山祈祓。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to perform the fengshan on Mount Tai and rain would not cease, the emperor had Daohe perform ritual prayer; soon it cleared, and he was ordered to ride post ahead to Mount Tai for purification rites.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared the fengshan on Mount Tai, unending rain fell; he had Daohe perform exorcistic rites, the sky soon cleared, and he was sent by relay post to Mount Tai to conduct purification ahead of the rites.

sentences.zh: 得賞賜輒散貧乏，無所蓄。

translations.literal: Whenever he received rewards he would give them to the poor, keeping nothing in store.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever rewards he received he gave to the destitute, hoarding nothing.

sentences.zh: 咸亨中，為帝作丹，劑成而卒。

translations.literal: In the Xianheng era he made elixir for the emperor; when the dose was complete he died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianheng period he compounded elixir for the emperor; when the batch was finished, he died.

sentences.zh: 帝后營宮，遷道合墓，開其棺，見骸坼若蟬蛻者。

translations.literal: Later, when the emperor built a palace, Daohe's tomb was moved; opening the coffin, they saw the bones split open like a cicada's slough.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while the emperor was building a palace, Daohe's tomb was opened; inside, the bones lay split as though a cicada had shed its shell.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，恨曰：「為我合丹，而自服去。」

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he said in regret: 'He made elixir for me, yet took it himself and left.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, the emperor said bitterly: 'He brewed elixir for me, then swallowed it himself and went away.

sentences.zh: 然所餘丹無它異。

translations.literal: Yet the elixir that remained showed no other marvel.
translations.idiomatic: The elixir left behind, however, showed no unusual power.

sentences.zh: 司馬承禎

translations.literal: Sima Chengzhen
translations.idiomatic: Sima Chengzhen

sentences.zh: 司馬承禎，字子微，洛州溫人。

translations.literal: Sima Chengzhen, styled Ziwei, was a man of Wen in Luo prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Chengzhen, courtesy name Ziwei, came from Wen in Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 事潘師正，傳辟穀道引術，無不通。

translations.literal: He studied under Pan Shizheng, transmitted the arts of grain avoidance and breath guidance, and was without anything he did not master.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Pan Shizheng, inherited techniques of abstaining from grain and guiding the breath, and left nothing unmastered.

sentences.zh: 師正異之，曰：「我得陶隱居正一法，逮而四世矣。」

translations.literal: Shizheng marveled at him and said: 'I received Lord Tao's Orthodox Unity method, and it has passed through four generations.
translations.idiomatic: Shizheng marveled at him, saying: 'I received Lord Tao Hongjing's Orthodox Unity teaching, and it has passed four generations to reach you.

sentences.zh: 因辭去，遍遊名山，廬天臺不出。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chengzhen left, traveled famous mountains everywhere, and built his hut on Tiantai without coming forth.
translations.idiomatic: Then Chengzhen departed, wandered every celebrated peak, and settled on Tiantai without emerging.

sentences.zh: 武后嘗召之，未幾，去。

translations.literal: Empress Wu once summoned him; before long he left.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu once summoned him; he stayed only briefly and was gone.

sentences.zh: 睿宗復命其兄承禕就起之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong again ordered his elder brother Chengyi to go and raise him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong again sent his elder brother Chengyi to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 既至，引入中掖廷問其術，對曰：「為道日損，損之又損，以至於無為。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was led into the central rear court and asked about his arts; he answered: 'In pursuing the Way, daily diminish; diminish again and again until you reach non-action.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, the emperor led him into the inner palace and asked about his teaching. He answered: 'In the Way one diminishes day by day—diminish again and again until there is nothing left to do.

sentences.zh: 夫心目所知見，每損之尚不能已，況攻異端而增智慮哉？」

translations.literal: What the eyes and mind know and see—even diminishing that cannot yet be stopped; how much less to attack heterodoxies and increase schemes and thought?
translations.idiomatic: What the eyes and mind know and see—even stripping that away is endless; how much less to chase strange doctrines and pile up cunning plans?

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「治身則爾，治國若何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'For governing the person it is so—but for governing the state, how?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: 'So for the self—but for governing the realm?'

sentences.zh: 對曰：「國猶身也，故游心於淡，合氣於漠，與物自然而無私焉，而天下治。」

translations.literal: He answered: 'The state is like the person; therefore let the heart roam in plainness, blend the breath with the vast, and with things be natural and without private ends—then all under Heaven is governed.'
translations.idiomatic: He replied: 'The realm is like the body. Let the heart dwell in simplicity, unite the breath with the vast silence, move with things as they are and without private ends—and the world orders itself.'

sentences.zh: 帝嗟味曰：「廣成之言也！」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed in appreciation and said: 'The words of Guangcheng!'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said: 'These are Guangcheng's words!'

sentences.zh: 錫寶琴、霞紋帔，還之。

translations.literal: He was granted a precious zither and a cloud-patterned stole, and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a precious zither and a cloud-woven robe, then sent home.

sentences.zh: 開元中，再被召至都，玄宗詔于王屋山置壇室以居。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he was again summoned to the capital; Emperor Xuanzong decreed that an altar chamber be built on Mount Wangwu for him to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan he was summoned to the capital once more; Emperor Xuanzong ordered an altar lodge built on Mount Wangwu for his residence.

sentences.zh: 善篆、隸，帝命以三體寫《老子》，刊正文句。

translations.literal: He excelled at seal and clerical script; the Emperor ordered him to write the Laozi in three script forms and to emend the text.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in seal and clerical calligraphy, he was commanded to transcribe the Laozi in three scripts and to correct its wording.

sentences.zh: 又命玉真公主及光祿卿韋縚至所居，按金籙，設祠，厚賜焉。

translations.literal: Again the Emperor ordered the Princess Yuzhen and the Director of Court Banquets Wei Chao to his dwelling to perform the Golden Register rites and set up sacrifices, and richly rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sent Princess Yuzhen and the Director of Court Banquets Wei Chao to his home to conduct Golden Register rituals and offerings, and lavished gifts upon him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十九，贈銀青光祿大夫，諡貞一先生，親文其碑。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-nine; posthumously he was given the Silver-Green-Glory Grand Master of the Palace and the posthumous title Master of Pure Unity; the emperor personally composed his epitaph.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-nine. The court granted him the posthumous rank of Silver-Green-Glory Grand Master of the Palace and the title Master of Pure Unity, and the emperor himself wrote his tomb inscription.

sentences.zh: 自師正、道合與承禎等，語言詼譎似方士，剟之不錄，直取其隱概云。

translations.literal: From Shi Zheng, Daohe, and Chengzhen onward, their speech was jesting and resembled that of immortality-seekers; these are cut and not recorded—only their reclusive outlines are taken.
translations.idiomatic: From Shi Zheng and Daohe through Chengzhen, their talk was witty and smacked of the wonder-workers; such material is omitted here, and only the broad outline of their withdrawal is preserved.

sentences.zh: 賀知章

translations.literal: He Zhizhang
translations.idiomatic: He Zhizhang

sentences.zh: 賀知章，字季真，越州永興人。

translations.literal: He Zhizhang, style name Jizhen, was a man of Yongxing in Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhizhang, courtesy name Jizhen, came from Yongxing in Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 性曠夷，善談說，與族姑子陸象先善。

translations.literal: By nature broad and easy, skilled at discourse, he was on good terms with his clanswoman's son Lu Xiangxian.
translations.idiomatic: Open and unencumbered by nature, a gifted talker, he was close to his cousin Lu Xiangxian.

sentences.zh: 象先嘗謂人曰：「季真清談風流，吾一日不見，則鄙吝生矣。」

translations.literal: Xiangxian once said to others: "Jizhen's pure talk and elegant manner—if I do not see him for a day, meanness rises in me."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiangxian once remarked, "One day without Jizhen's refined conversation and easy grace, and I turn petty again."

sentences.zh: 證聖初，擢進士、超拔群類科，累遷太常博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhengsheng era he was selected as jinshi and in the Outstanding Among All Categories examination, and was promoted repeatedly to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengsheng he passed the jinshi examination and the special "Outstanding Among All Categories" test, rising step by step to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 張說為麗正殿修書使，表知章及徐堅、趙冬曦入院，撰《六典》等書，累年無功。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue, as Commissioner for Editing Books at the Lizheng Hall, memorialized that Zhizhang together with Xu Jian and Zhao Dongxi enter the institute to compile the Six Codes and other works; for years there was no achievement.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yue headed the Lizheng Hall book project, he had Zhizhang, Xu Jian, and Zhao Dongxi join the staff to compile the Six Codes and related works, but after years little was finished.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年，遷禮部侍郎，兼集賢院學士，一日並謝。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan he was moved to Vice Minister of Rites and concurrently Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and on one day received thanks for both appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 13 he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites and concurrently a Hanlin academician, receiving both honors in a single audience of thanks.

sentences.zh: 宰相源乾曜語說曰：「賀公兩命之榮，足為光寵，然學士、侍郎孰為美？」

translations.literal: Chief Minister Yuan Qianyao said to Yue: "Sir He's double honor is glory enough—but which is finer, academician or vice minister?
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister Yuan Qianyao asked Zhang Yue, "Master He has two honors at once—splendid—but which is the greater, academician or vice minister?

sentences.zh: 說曰：「侍郎衣冠之選，然要為具員吏；

translations.literal: Yue said: "Vice minister is the choice of official robes; yet in the end it is a post filled as a matter of course.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue replied, "Vice minister is the pick of the robed bureaucracy, yet in the end it is still a seat anyone can fill.

sentences.zh: 學士懷先王之道，經緯之文，然後處之。

translations.literal: The academician holds the way of the former kings and the warp and woof of letters—only then is he placed there.
translations.idiomatic: The academician must carry the way of the ancient kings and the weave of classical writing—only then does he belong there.

sentences.zh: 此其為間也。」

translations.literal: This is the distance between them.
translations.idiomatic: That is the difference between the two.

sentences.zh: 玄宗自為贊賜之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong himself composed a laudation and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong wrote a commendation in his own hand and presented it to him.

sentences.zh: 遷太子右庶子，充侍讀。

translations.literal: He was moved to Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household and appointed attendant reader.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household and made a lecturing attendant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 申王薨，詔選挽郎，而知章取捨不平，廕子喧訴不能止，知章梯牆出首以決事，人皆靳之，坐徙工部。

translations.literal: When Prince Shen died, an edict chose dirge-singers; Zhizhang's selections were unfair, and yinzi clamored in appeal and could not be stopped; Zhizhang climbed the wall and stuck out his head to settle the matter—everyone was critical of him, and as punishment he was transferred to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Shen's death, the court chose funeral singers; Zhizhang's picks were biased, and officials' sons raised such a clamor of protest that he had to climb the wall and lean over it to settle the dispute. People sneered at him, and he was demoted to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 肅宗為太子，知章遷賓客，授秘書監，而左補闕薛令之兼侍讀。

translations.literal: When Suzong was crown prince, Zhizhang was moved to Palace Guest and given the post of Director of the Palace Library, while Left Remonstrator Xue Lingzhi served concurrently as lecturing attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong was heir apparent, Zhizhang became a palace guest and Director of the Palace Library, with Left Remonstrator Xue Lingzhi as co-lecturer.

sentences.zh: 時東宮官積年不遷，令之書壁，望禮之薄，帝見，復題「聽自安者」。

translations.literal: At that time eastern-palace officials had gone years without promotion; Lingzhi wrote on the wall that he looked on the thinness of ritual regard; the emperor saw it and added the words "Hear and be at peace."
translations.idiomatic: Eastern-palace staff had gone years without promotion. Lingzhi wrote on a wall that he found the court's regard too slight; the emperor saw it and added, "Hear this and rest content."

sentences.zh: 令之即棄官，徒步歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Lingzhi at once abandoned office and walked home to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhi immediately resigned and walked home on foot.

sentences.zh: 知章晚節尤誕放，遨嬉裏巷，自號「四明狂客」及「秘書外監」。

translations.literal: In his late years Zhizhang was especially unrestrained and playful, roaming the lanes in sport, styling himself "Mad Guest of Siming" and "Outer Overseer of the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: In old age he grew wilder still, carousing in the alleys and calling himself the "Mad Guest of Siming" and the "Outer Overseer of the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 每醉，輒屬辭，筆不停書，咸有可觀，未始刊飭。

translations.literal: Whenever drunk he would compose in succession; the brush did not stop, and all were worth viewing—never once did he revise or polish.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, he would pour out verse after verse without pause; everything he wrote was striking, and he never revised a line.

sentences.zh: 善草隸，好事者具筆研從之，意有所愜，不復拒，然紙才十數字，世傳以為寶。

translations.literal: Skilled in cursive and clerical script, enthusiasts supplied brush and ink and followed him; when his mood was pleased he did not refuse, yet the paper held only a dozen characters or so—the world transmitted them as treasures.
translations.idiomatic: A master of cursive and clerical script, admirers brought him brush and ink wherever he went. When the mood took him he would not refuse, though he rarely wrote more than a dozen characters—and those scraps were treasured as heirlooms.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，病，夢游帝居，數日寤，乃請為道士，還鄉里，詔許之，以宅為千秋觀而居。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he fell ill, dreamed of wandering the emperor's abode, and after several days awoke; then he asked to become a Daoist priest and return home, and an edict permitted it; his residence was made the Qianqiu Abbey where he dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era he fell ill, dreamed he wandered the imperial palace, and woke after several days. He then asked to take Daoist orders and go home; the emperor agreed and turned his house into the Qianqiu Abbey for his retirement.

sentences.zh: 又求周宮湖數頃為放生池，有詔賜鏡湖剡川一曲。

translations.literal: He also asked for several qing of Zhou Palace Lake as a release-life pool; an edict granted him a bend of Mirror Lake and Shanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested a tract of Zhou Palace Lake as a pond for releasing captive animals; the throne instead granted him a stretch of Mirror Lake and the Shanchuan stream.

sentences.zh: 既行，帝賜詩，皇太子百官餞送。

translations.literal: When he set out, the emperor bestowed a poem; the crown prince and all officials saw him off.
translations.idiomatic: On his departure the emperor gave him a parting poem, and the crown prince and the whole court escorted him.

sentences.zh: 擢其子僧子為會稽郡司馬，賜緋魚，使侍養，幼子亦聽為道士。

translations.literal: His son Sengzi was promoted to Siming Prefecture assistant magistrate, given crimson robe and fish tally to attend him in his support, and the younger son was also permitted to become a Daoist priest.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sengzi was made assistant magistrate of Kuaiji to support him, given crimson robes and the fish tally of rank, and his younger son was allowed to become a Daoist priest as well.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十六。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 肅宗乾元初，以雅舊，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyuan under Suzong, because of old elegance he was posthumously given Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianyuan, Suzong posthumously made him Minister of Rites in remembrance of their long friendship.

sentences.zh: 令之，長溪人。

translations.literal: Lingzhi was a man of Changxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Lingzhi was from Changxi.

sentences.zh: 肅宗亦以舊恩召，而令之已前卒。

translations.literal: Suzong also summoned him for old favor, but Lingzhi had already died earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong meant to summon him too out of old regard, but Lingzhi had already died.

sentences.zh: 秦系，字公緒，越州會稽人。

translations.literal: Qin Xi, style name Gongxu, was a man of Kuaiji in Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Xi, courtesy name Gongxu, was from Kuaiji in Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，避亂剡溪，北都留守薛兼訓奏為右衛率府倉曹參軍，不就。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he fled turmoil to Shaxi; the Beidu garrison commander Xue Jianxun memorialized him as Army Aide in the Right Guard Rate Office—he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tianbao disorders broke out he fled to Shaxi. Xue Jianxun, commander of the northern capital garrison, recommended him as aide in the Right Guard Rate Office, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 客泉州，南安有九日山，大松百餘章，俗傳東晉時所植，系結廬其上，穴石為研，注《老子》，彌年不出。

translations.literal: As a guest in Quanzhou, at Nan'an there is Nine-Peak Mountain with more than a hundred great pines, popularly said to have been planted in Eastern Jin times; Xi built a hut on it, hollowed stone for an inkstone, annotated the Laozi, and for a full year did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Living in Quanzhou, he settled on Nine Peaks at Nan'an, where folk said more than a hundred ancient pines had stood since Eastern Jin. He built a hut among them, carved an inkstone from the rock, worked on the Laozi, and did not emerge for a year.

sentences.zh: 刺史薛播數往見之，歲時致羊酒，而系未嘗至城門。

translations.literal: Prefect Xue Bo several times went to see him; at the seasons he sent mutton and wine, yet Xi never once came to the city gate.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Xue Bo visited repeatedly and sent wine and mutton at the festivals, but Xi never once entered the city gate.

sentences.zh: 薑公輔之謫，見系輒窮日不能去，築室與相近，忘流落之苦。

translations.literal: When Jiang Gongfu was banished, on seeing Xi he could not leave all day; he built a house near him and forgot the bitterness of exile.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Gongfu was exiled, a single meeting with Xi held him all day; he built a cottage nearby and forgot the misery of banishment.

sentences.zh: 公輔卒，妻子在遠，系為葬山下。

translations.literal: When Gongfu died his wife and children were far away; Xi buried him below the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: After Gongfu died, with his family far away, Xi buried him at the foot of the mountain.

sentences.zh: 張建封聞系之不可致，請就加校書郎。

translations.literal: Zhang Jianfeng, hearing that Xi could not be summoned, asked that he be given the added title of Proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianfeng, learning that Xi could not be lured to office, had him appointed proofreader in absentia.

sentences.zh: 與劉長卿善，以詩相贈答。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Liu Changqing and exchanged poems.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Liu Changqing and they exchanged poems.

sentences.zh: 權德輿曰：「長卿自以為五言長城，系用偏師攻之，雖老益壯。」

translations.literal: Quan Deyu said: "Changqing considered himself a Great Wall of five-character verse; Xi attacked with a flanking force—and though old, he grew only bolder.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Deyu wrote, "Changqing thought himself a Great Wall of pentasyllabic verse; Xi assailed him with a flanking army—and in age he only fought harder.

sentences.zh: 其後東度秣陵，年八十餘卒。

translations.literal: Later he went east across Moling and died past eighty.
translations.idiomatic: Later he crossed east to Moling and died in his eighties.

sentences.zh: 南安人思之，為立於亭，號其山為高士峰云。

translations.literal: The people of Nan'an missed him and set up a pavilion for him, calling the mountain Lofty Gentleman's Peak.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Nan'an honored him with a pavilion and named the peak Lofty Gentleman's Peak.

sentences.zh: 張志和

translations.literal: Zhang Zhike
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhike

sentences.zh: 張志和，字子同，婺州金華人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhike, style name Zitong, was a man of Jinhua in Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhike, courtesy name Zitong, came from Jinhua in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 始名龜齡。

translations.literal: His original name was Gui Ling.
translations.idiomatic: He was born Zhang Guiling.

sentences.zh: 父游朝，通莊、列二子書，為《象罔》、《白馬證》諸篇佐其說。

translations.literal: His father Youchao mastered the books of Zhuangzi and Liezi and wrote such pieces as "Elephant Without" and "White Horse Proof" to support their doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: His father Youchao was steeped in Zhuangzi and Liezi and wrote essays such as "Elephant Without" and "White Horse Proof" to expound their teaching.

sentences.zh: 母夢楓生腹上而產志和。

translations.literal: His mother dreamed a maple growing on her belly and bore Zhike.
translations.idiomatic: His mother dreamed a maple tree sprouting from her belly before he was born.

sentences.zh: 十六擢明經，以策幹肅宗，特見賞重，命待詔翰林，授左金吾衛錄事參軍，因賜名。

translations.literal: At sixteen he passed the Mingjing examination; with policy essays he impressed Suzong, who especially valued him, ordered him to await edicts at the Hanlin, appointed him Recorder in the Left Golden Crow Guard, and bestowed his present name.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he passed the Mingjing examination. His policy essays won Suzong's special favor; he was kept at Hanlin awaiting edicts, made recorder in the Left Golden Crow Guard, and given the name Zhike.

sentences.zh: 後坐事貶南浦尉，會赦還，以親既喪，不復仕，居江湖，自稱煙波釣徒。

translations.literal: Later for an offense he was demoted to magistrate of Nanpu; when an amnesty returned him, his parents having died he did not take office again; he lived on rivers and lakes and called himself the Angler of Misty Waves.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was banished to magistrate of Nanpu. After an amnesty brought him back, both parents were dead and he never served again. He lived on the waterways and called himself the Angler of Misty Waves.

sentences.zh: 著《玄真子》，亦以自號。

translations.literal: He wrote the Xuanzhenzi and also took it as his style.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Xuanzhenzi and took that as his sobriquet as well.

sentences.zh: 有韋詣者，為撰《內解》。

translations.literal: A certain Wei Gai wrote an Inner Explication for him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gai composed an "Inner Explication" for his work.

sentences.zh: 志和又著《太易》十五篇，其卦三百六十五。

translations.literal: Zhike also wrote fifteen chapters of the Great Changes, its hexagrams numbering three hundred sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote fifteen chapters on the Changes, with all three hundred sixty-five hexagrams.

sentences.zh: 兄鶴齡恐其遁世不還，為築室越州東郭，茨以生草，椽棟不施斤斧。

translations.literal: His elder brother Heling feared he would flee the world and not return, and for him built a house east of the city in Yuezhou, thatched with living grass, rafters and beams untouched by axe.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Heling, fearing he would vanish into reclusion forever, built him a cottage east of Yuezhou city, thatched with living turf, its timbers left uncut by any axe.

sentences.zh: 豹席棕〓，每垂釣不設餌，志不在魚也。

translations.literal: Leopard-skin mats and palm-fiber sandals—each time he angled he set no bait; his aim was not fish.
translations.idiomatic: He sat on leopard skins and wore palm-fiber sandals; when he fished he used no bait, for fish were never the point.

sentences.zh: 縣令使浚渠，執畚無忤色。

translations.literal: The magistrate had him dredge a canal; he took the basket and showed no offended color.
translations.idiomatic: When the county magistrate put him to dredging a canal, he took up the hod without a trace of resentment.

sentences.zh: 嘗欲以大布制裘，嫂為躬績織，及成，衣之，雖暑不解。

translations.literal: Once he wished to make a great-cloth coat; his sister-in-law personally spun and wove it, and when it was done he wore it and would not remove it even in summer heat.
translations.idiomatic: He once wanted a coat of coarse cloth; his sister-in-law spun and wove it herself, and when it was finished he wore it through the hottest summer without taking it off.

sentences.zh: 觀察使陳少遊往見，為終日留，表其居曰玄真坊。

translations.literal: Observation Commissioner Chen Shaoyou went to see him, stayed a whole day, and memorialized that his residence be named Xuanzhen Ward.
translations.idiomatic: Regional inspector Chen Shaoyou visited, stayed the full day, and had his quarter officially named Xuanzhen Ward.

sentences.zh: 以門隘，為買地大其閎，號回軒巷。

translations.literal: Because the gate was narrow, he bought land to enlarge the breadth and called it Turning-Pavilion Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the gate too narrow, Shaoyou bought land to widen the compound and named the lane Turning-Pavilion Alley.

sentences.zh: 先是門阻流水，無梁，少遊為構之，人號大夫橋。

translations.literal: Earlier the gate was blocked by flowing water without a bridge; Shaoyou built one for him, and people called it the Grandee's Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Before that, a stream blocked the door and there was no bridge; Shaoyou built one, and people called it the Grandee's Bridge.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗賜奴婢各一，志和配為夫婦，號漁童、樵青。

translations.literal: The emperor once bestowed a male and female slave; Zhike paired them as husband and wife and called them Fisher Boy and Woodcutter Green.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once gave him a male and female servant; Zhike married them to each other and named them Fisher Boy and Woodcutter Green.

sentences.zh: 陸羽常問：「孰為往來者？」

translations.literal: Lu Yu often asked: "Who are your comings and goings?
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu once asked him, "Who are your visitors?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「太虛為室，明月為燭，與四海諸公共處，未嘗少別也，何有往來？」

translations.literal: He answered: "The Great Void is my room, the bright moon my lamp; I dwell with all within the four seas and have never been parted even briefly—what comings and goings are there?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The void is my hall and the bright moon my lamp. I keep company with everyone under heaven and am never apart from them—what visitors do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 顏真卿為湖州刺史值志和來謁，真卿以舟敝漏，請更之，志和曰：「願為浮家泛宅，往來苕、霅間。」

translations.literal: Yan Zhenqing, as prefect of Huzhou when Zhike came to call, said the boat was worn and leaking and asked to replace it; Zhike said: "I wish to be a floating home on drifting waters, coming and going between Tiao and Zha."
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Zhenqing was prefect of Huzhou and Zhike came to visit, Zhenqing offered to replace his leaky boat. Zhike answered, "I mean to be a floating home on the currents, roaming between the Tiao and Zha rivers."

sentences.zh: 辯捷類如此。

translations.literal: His quick wit was of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His wit ran in that vein.

sentences.zh: 善圖山水，酒酣，或擊鼓吹笛，舐筆輒成。

translations.literal: Skilled at landscape painting, when wine was warm he would sometimes beat drums, blow pipes, or lick the brush and complete a work at once.
translations.idiomatic: He painted landscapes masterfully; drunk, he might drum, play the flute, or wet the brush with his tongue and finish a painting on the spot.

sentences.zh: 嘗撰《漁歌》，憲宗圖真求其歌，不能致。

translations.literal: Once he composed Fisher Songs; Emperor Xianzong had a true likeness made and sought the songs but could not obtain them.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote Fisher Songs; Emperor Xianzong had his portrait painted and asked for the songs but could not get them.

sentences.zh: 李德裕稱志和「隱而有名，顯而無事，不窮不達，嚴光之比」云。

translations.literal: Li Deyu praised Zhike as "hidden yet famous, visible yet without affairs, neither destitute nor eminent—a peer of Yan Guang."
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu said of him, "Reclusive yet renowned, in the world yet unencumbered—neither poor nor grand—a man in the mold of Yan Guang."

sentences.zh: 孫述睿

translations.literal: Sun Shurui
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shurui

sentences.zh: 孫述睿，越州山陰人。

translations.literal: Sun Shurui was a man of Shanyin in Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shurui was from Shanyin in Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 梁侍中休源八世孫。

translations.literal: Eighth-generation descendant of Sun Xiuyuan, Attendant-in-Ordinary of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He was the eighth-generation descendant of Liang's Attendant-in-Ordinary Sun Xiuyuan.

sentences.zh: 高祖德紹，事竇建德為中書侍郎，嘗草檄毀薄太宗，賊平，執登汜水樓，責曰：「爾以檄謗我云何？」

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Deshao served Dou Jiande as Vice Director of the Secretariat; he once drafted a proclamation slandering Taizong; when the bandits were pacified he was seized and brought up the Sishui Tower; Taizong reproached him: "You slandered me in your proclamation—how so?
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Deshao had served Dou Jiande as vice director of the secretariat and once drafted a proclamation vilifying Taizong. After the rebellion was crushed he was taken to the top of Sishui Tower, where Taizong demanded, "You reviled me in that dispatch—how do you answer?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「犬吠非其主。」

translations.literal: He replied: "A dog barks—not at its own master."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "A dog barks at whoever is not his master."

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「賊乃主邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: "So the bandit was your master?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flared up: "Then the rebel was your master?"

sentences.zh: 命壯士捽殞樓下。

translations.literal: He ordered strong men to dash him to death below the tower.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered brawny guards to hurl him from the tower to his death.

sentences.zh: 曾祖昌寓，字廣成，貞觀中對策高第，歷魏州司馬，有治狀，帝為不置刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Changyu, style Guangcheng, in Zhenguan took first place in the policy examination, served as Sima of Weizhou with marked good governance, and the emperor for that reason did not appoint a prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Changyu, courtesy name Guangcheng, took top honors in the Zhenguan policy examination, served as Weizhou vice prefect with such distinction that the throne left the prefecture without a separate prefect.

sentences.zh: 為政三年，璽書褒美，進膳部郎中。

translations.literal: After three years in office an imperial letter praised him and he was advanced to Director in the Ministry of Provisions.
translations.idiomatic: After three years an imperial commendation raised him to director in the Ministry of Provisions.

sentences.zh: 祖祖舜，字奉先，為監察御史，以累下除成武令，雉馴於廷。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zushun, style Fengxian, was Investigating Censor; for cumulative faults he was demoted to magistrate of Chengwu, and pheasants were tame in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zushun, courtesy name Fengxian, was an investigating censor; demoted for repeated faults to magistrate of Chengwu, he governed so gently that pheasants grew tame in his courtyard.

sentences.zh: 述睿少與兄充符、弟克讓篤孝，已孤，偕隱嵩山。

translations.literal: Shurui in youth with his elder brother Chongfu and younger brother Kerang were deeply filial; already orphaned, they withdrew together to Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Shurui, his elder brother Chongfu, and his younger brother Kerang were models of filial piety; orphaned, they retired together to Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 而述睿資嗜學。

translations.literal: Yet Shurui by nature loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shurui was devoted to study by nature.

sentences.zh: 大曆中，劉晏薦于代宗，乙太常寺協律郎召，擢累司勳員外郎、史館修撰。

translations.literal: In the Dali era Liu Yan recommended him to Emperor Daizong; summoned as Vice Director of Music in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices on the second rank list, he was promoted through repeated posts to Vice Director in the Ministry of Honors and Compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: During Dali, Liu Yan recommended him to Daizong; summoned as vice director of music and then steadily promoted, he became vice director in the Ministry of Honors and a historiography compiler.

sentences.zh: 述睿每一遷，即至朝謝。

translations.literal: Each time Shurui was promoted he would go to court to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Every promotion brought Shurui to court to give thanks in person.

sentences.zh: 俄而辭疾歸，以為常。

translations.literal: Soon he pleaded illness and returned, and this became his custom.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he would plead illness and go home again—his lifelong pattern.

sentences.zh: 德宗立，拜諫議大夫，命河南尹趙惠伯齎詔書束帛，備禮敦遣。

translations.literal: When Dezong took the throne he was made Remonstrator; the Henan governor Zhao Huibo was ordered to carry the edict, silks, and full rites to urge him earnestly.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong ascended the throne he was made remonstrator; Henan governor Zhao Huibo was sent with edict, silks, and full ceremony to press him to accept.

sentences.zh: 既至，對別殿，賜第宅，給廄馬，兼皇太子侍讀。

translations.literal: When he arrived he was received in a separate hall, given a mansion, supplied stable horses, and made concurrently lecturer to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he was received in a side hall, given a mansion and stable horses, and appointed lecturer to the crown prince as well.

sentences.zh: 固辭，弗許。

translations.literal: He firmly declined; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He refused firmly; the court would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 久乃改秘書少監，兼右庶子，復為史館修撰。

translations.literal: After a long while he was changed to Vice Director of the Palace Library and concurrently Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household, and again became a historiography compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long interval was he moved to vice director of the palace library and right vice director of the crown prince's household, again as historiography compiler.

sentences.zh: 述睿重次《地理志》，本末最詳。

translations.literal: Shurui recompiled the Geographic Treatise; beginning and end were most detailed.
translations.idiomatic: He reorganized the Geographic Treatise with unmatched thoroughness from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 性退讓，未始忤物，雖親朋燕集，至嚴默終日，人皆畏之。

translations.literal: By nature yielding, he never once offended others; even at intimate gatherings of kin and friends he would sit sternly silent all day, and people all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Humble by nature, he never gave offense; even at family feasts he sat in grave silence all day, and people stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 與令狐峘同職，峘數抵侮，然卒不校也，時稱長者。

translations.literal: He shared office with Linghu Di; Di several times insulted him, yet in the end he never quarreled—of the time he was called an elder.
translations.idiomatic: He served with Linghu Di, who often insulted him, yet he never answered back and was known as a man of forbearance.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年，帝念平涼之難尤惻怛，以述睿精愨而誠，故遣持祠具稱詔臨祭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan the emperor, thinking especially of the Pingliang disaster with deep grief, because Shurui was precise and sincere sent him with ritual vessels to proclaim the edict and perform the sacrifice in person.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 4, still anguished over the Pingliang disaster, the emperor sent him—with full ritual gear and an edict in hand—to offer sacrifice in person, trusting his scrupulous loyalty.

sentences.zh: 又以疾乞解，久乃許，以太子賓客還鄉，賜帛五十匹、衣一襲。

translations.literal: Again he begged to be released for illness; only after long delay was it granted; he was made Crown Prince's Guest and returned home, granted fifty bolts of silk and one suit of clothes.
translations.idiomatic: He again begged leave on grounds of illness; only after long delay was he allowed to go home as crown prince's guest, with fifty bolts of silk and a suit of robes.

sentences.zh: 故事，致仕不給公馹，帝特命給焉。

translations.literal: By precedent, on retirement one was not given official relay horses; the emperor specially ordered them given.
translations.idiomatic: By custom retired officials received no post horses; the emperor made an exception for him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十一，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-one; posthumously he was given Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-one and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子敏行，字至之。

translations.literal: His son Minxing, style Zhizhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Minxing, courtesy name Zhizhi.

sentences.zh: 元和初，擢進士第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhe era he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 岳鄂呂元膺表在節度府，元膺徙東都、河中，輒隨府遷。

translations.literal: Lü Yuanfu of Yue-E memorialized him for service in the military governorship; when Yuanfu moved to the eastern capital and to Hezhong, Minxing followed the office each time.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yuanfu of Yue-E brought him into his staff; when Yuanfu was transferred to the eastern capital and then to Hezhong, Minxing followed each move.

sentences.zh: 入拜右拾遺，四遷司勳郎中、集賢殿學士、諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He entered court as Right Remembrancer, was promoted four times to Director in the Ministry of Honors, Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as right remembrancer and rose through four posts to director in the Ministry of Honors, Hanlin academician, and remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 李絳遇害，事本監軍楊叔元，時無敢言，敏行上書極論之，叔元乃得罪。

translations.literal: When Li Jiang was murdered the affair originated with the army supervisor Yang Shuyuan; at the time none dared speak; Minxing memorialized with extreme argument and Shuyuan was punished.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jiang was assassinated the trail led to army supervisor Yang Shuyuan, and no one dared speak; Minxing submitted a fierce memorial and Shuyuan was punished.

sentences.zh: 以名臣子，少修潔，及仕宦，能交當時豪俊，有名一時，而雅操不逮父矣。

translations.literal: As the son of a famous minister, in youth he cultivated purity; in official life he could befriend the mighty of the age and for a time had a name, yet in elegant conduct he did not reach his father.
translations.idiomatic: A famous minister's son, he kept himself clean in youth and in office moved among the great men of the day, winning renown for a time—but in moral stature he never matched his father.

sentences.zh: 卒，年三十九，贈工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He died at age thirty-nine; posthumously he was given Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-nine and was posthumously made Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 陸羽，字鴻漸，一名疾，字季疵，復州竟陵人。

translations.literal: Lu Yu, style Hongjian, also named Ji, style Jici, was a man of Jingling in Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu, courtesy name Hongjian, also called Ji and Jici, was from Jingling in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 不知所生，或言有僧得諸水濱，畜之。

translations.literal: No one knew where he was born; some say a monk found him by the waterside and reared him.
translations.idiomatic: No one knew his birth; some said a monk found him beside the water and raised him.

sentences.zh: 既長，以《易》自筮，得《蹇》之《漸》，曰：「鴻漸于陸，其羽可用為儀。」

translations.literal: When grown he divined by the Changes and obtained the Gradual in the Obstruction, saying: "The wild goose gradually approaches the land; its feathers may serve as ritual vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he cast the Changes and drew Gradual within Obstruction: "The wild goose advances onto the land; its feathers may serve as ritual regalia.

sentences.zh: 乃以陸為氏，名而字之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took Lu as surname and Hongjian as given name and style.
translations.idiomatic: He took Lu as his surname and Hongjian as his name and courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 幼時，其師教以旁行書，答曰：「終鮮兄弟，而絕後嗣，得為孝乎？」

translations.literal: In childhood his teacher taught him to write in vertical columns; he answered: "In the end few brothers, and cut off posterity—can this be filial?
translations.idiomatic: As a boy his teacher had him practice vertical script; he replied, "Few brothers in the end, and no heirs—is that filial?

sentences.zh: 師怒，使執糞除圬塓以苦之，又使牧牛三十，羽潛以竹畫牛背為字。

translations.literal: The teacher in anger had him carry dung and plaster walls to torment him, and also had him herd thirty cattle; Yu secretly used bamboo to draw characters on the oxen's backs.
translations.idiomatic: The teacher, furious, set him to hauling night soil and daubing walls, and made him tend thirty oxen; Yu secretly scratched characters on their backs with bamboo slips.

sentences.zh: 得張衡《南都賦》，不能讀，危坐效群兒囁嚅若成誦狀，師拘之，令薙草莽。

translations.literal: He obtained Zhang Heng's Rhapsody on the Southern Capital; unable to read it, he sat upright imitating the children in murmuring as if completing recitation; the teacher bound him and ordered him to cut grass and brambles.
translations.idiomatic: He got hold of Zhang Heng's Rhapsody on the Southern Capital; unable to read it, he sat stiffly mimicking the other boys' mumbling as though he knew it by heart. The teacher tied him up and set him to clearing brush.

sentences.zh: 當其記文字，懵懵若有遺，過日不作，主者鞭苦，因歎曰：「歲月往矣，奈何不知書！」

translations.literal: When he was to memorize characters he was dazed as if something were lost; if for a day he did not compose, the master whipped him cruelly; he therefore sighed: "The years go—how can I not know books!
translations.idiomatic: When set to memorize text he stared blankly as though something were missing; if he produced nothing in a day the master beat him savagely. He burst out, "The years are slipping away—how can I still be illiterate!

sentences.zh: 嗚咽不自勝，因亡去，匿為優人，作詼諧數千言。

translations.literal: He sobbed uncontrollably, fled, hid himself as a comic actor, and composed several thousand words of jest.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, he ran away, joined a troupe of jesters, and wrote several thousand lines of comic verse.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，州人酺，吏署羽伶師，太守李齊物見，異之，授以書，遂廬火門山。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era the people of the prefecture held a communal feast; the clerk assigned Yu as troupe master; Prefect Li Qiwu saw him, marveled at him, and gave him books; then he lodged on Huomen Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao the prefecture held a public feast; the clerk made Yu master of ceremonies. Prefect Li Qiwu saw him, was struck by him, and gave him books; he then lived as a recluse on Huomen Mountain.

sentences.zh: 貌侻陋，口吃而辯。

translations.literal: In appearance he was homely and odd, stammering yet eloquent.
translations.idiomatic: Ugly and eccentric in looks, he stammered yet argued brilliantly.

sentences.zh: 聞人善，若在己，見有過者，規切至忤人。

translations.literal: Hearing of others' excellence was as if it were his own; seeing one who had faults he admonished to the point of offending.
translations.idiomatic: He rejoiced in others' gifts as though they were his own and rebuked wrongdoing so bluntly that he gave offense.

sentences.zh: 朋友燕處，意有所行輒去，人疑其多嗔。

translations.literal: At friends' gatherings, if something in his mind moved him he would leave; people suspected him of much anger.
translations.idiomatic: At gatherings of friends he would walk out the moment the mood struck him; people thought him quick to wrath.

sentences.zh: 與人期，雨雪虎狼不避也。

translations.literal: When he made appointments he did not avoid snow, rain, tigers, or wolves.
translations.idiomatic: He kept appointments through snow, rain, tigers, and wolves alike.

sentences.zh: 上元初，更隱苕溪，自稱桑苧翁，闔門著書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shangyuan he withdrew further to Tiao Creek, styled himself Old Man of the Mulberry and Hemp, and with closed doors wrote books.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shangyuan era he retired deeper to Tiaoxi, called himself the Old Man of Mulberry and Hemp, and wrote behind closed doors.

sentences.zh: 或獨行野中，誦詩擊木，裴回不得意，或慟哭而歸，故時謂今接輿也。

translations.literal: Sometimes walking alone in the wild he would recite poetry and beat wood; pacing, unable to find his intent, or weeping he would return—so of the time they called him the present Jieyu.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he wandered alone in the countryside chanting verse and beating a clapper; unable to settle his mind he would circle back weeping—and men called him the Jieyu of his age.

sentences.zh: 久之，詔拜羽太子文學，徙太常寺太祝，不就職。

translations.literal: After long time an edict appointed Yu Literary Attendant to the Crown Prince and moved him to Sacrificial Official in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually an edict made him literary attendant to the crown prince and then sacrificial official in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he accepted neither post.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，卒。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died near the end of the Zhenyuan era.

sentences.zh: 羽嗜茶，著經三篇，言茶之原、之法、之具尤備，天下益知飲茶矣。

translations.literal: Yu loved tea and wrote three classic chapters; on tea's origin, methods, and implements he was especially complete, and the empire came increasingly to know drinking tea.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu loved tea and wrote three classic treatises on its origin, preparation, and utensils so fully that the empire learned to drink tea through him.

sentences.zh: 時鬻茶者，至陶羽形置煬突間，祀為茶神。

translations.literal: Tea sellers of the time even cast Yu's image and placed it in the stove flue, worshipping him as the god of tea.
translations.idiomatic: Tea merchants cast his image and set it in their stove vents, worshipping him as the god of tea.

sentences.zh: 有常伯熊者，因羽論復廣著茶之功。

translations.literal: There was Chang Boxiong, who because of Yu's treatise further broadly wrote on tea's merits.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Boxiong, building on Yu's work, wrote at greater length on the virtues of tea.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫李季卿宣慰江南，次臨淮，知伯熊善煮茶，召之，伯熊執器前，季卿為再舉杯。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Li Jiqing, on pacification tour in Jiangnan, stopped at Linhuai; learning Boxiong brewed tea well, he summoned him; Boxiong came forward with vessels and Jiqing raised his cup twice.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Li Jiqing, touring Jiangnan, stopped at Linhuai; told that Boxiong brewed tea superbly, he summoned him; Boxiong came forward with his implements and Jiqing drank two cups in his honor.

sentences.zh: 至江南，又有薦羽者，召之，羽衣野服，挈具而入，季卿不為禮，羽愧之，更著《毀茶論》。

translations.literal: Reaching Jiangnan, another recommended Yu; he was summoned; Yu in rustic dress entered carrying his gear; Jiqing did not show ritual courtesy; Yu was shamed and further wrote On the Ruin of Tea.
translations.idiomatic: Farther south someone recommended Lu Yu; he was summoned. Yu entered in country clothes with his tea kit; Jiqing showed no courtesy. Mortified, Yu wrote On the Ruin of Tea.

sentences.zh: 其後尚茶成風，時回紇入朝，始驅馬市茶。

translations.literal: Afterward esteem for tea became a fashion; at the time the Uyghurs came to court and first drove horses to trade for tea.
translations.idiomatic: Tea fashion spread; when the Uyghurs came to court they first drove horses to market to buy tea.

sentences.zh: 崔覲，梁州城固人。

translations.literal: Cui Guan was a man of Chenggu in Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guan was from Chenggu in Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以儒自業，身耕耨取給。

translations.literal: He took Confucian learning as his profession and by his own plowing and hoeing supplied his needs.
translations.idiomatic: He lived by Confucian study and fed himself with his own hoe.

sentences.zh: 老無子，乃以田宅財貲分給奴婢各為業，而身與妻隱南山，約奴婢過其舍則給酒食，夫婦嘯詠相視為娛。

translations.literal: Old and without sons, he then divided fields, houses, and wealth among male and female slaves each for their livelihood, while he and his wife withdrew to the southern mountains; they agreed that when slaves passed their dwelling they would supply food and drink; husband and wife whistled and chanted, gazing at each other for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Childless in old age, he divided fields, house, and goods among his servants so each could make a living, then he and his wife retired to the southern hills. Servants who passed their hut were fed; the couple amused themselves with songs and whistles, content in each other's company.

sentences.zh: 山南西道節度使鄭余慶辟為參謀，敦趣就職，不曉吏事，余慶稱長者。

translations.literal: Shannan West Circuit military governor Zheng Yuqing recruited him as staff planner, urgently urging him to take office; he did not understand clerkly affairs; Yuqing called him an elder.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuqing, military governor of Shannan West, made him a staff adviser and pressed him to serve; Guan knew nothing of bureaucratic business, and Yuqing called him a man of virtue.

sentences.zh: 文宗時，左補厥王直方，其里中人也，上書論事，見便殿，訪遺逸，直方薦覲高行，詔以起居郎召，辭疾不至。

translations.literal: In Wenzong's time Left Remonstrator Wang Zhifang, a man of his native place, memorialized on affairs, was received in the Convenient Hall; the emperor inquired after recluses; Zhifang recommended Guan's lofty conduct; an edict summoned him as Attendant Gentleman—he pleaded illness and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wenzong, Left Remonstrator Wang Zhifang, a fellow townsman, was heard in the Convenient Hall on state affairs; asked about hidden worthies he praised Guan's conduct. The throne summoned him as attendant gentleman; he pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 陸龜蒙

translations.literal: Lu Guimeng
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guimeng

sentences.zh: 陸龜蒙，字魯望，元方七世孫也。

translations.literal: Lu Guimeng, style Luwang, was seventh-generation descendant of Lu Yuanfang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guimeng, courtesy name Luwang, was the seventh-generation descendant of Lu Yuanfang.

sentences.zh: 父賓虞，以文曆侍御史。

translations.literal: His father Binyu served as Attendant Censor through literary office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Binyu had been an attendant censor distinguished for his writing.

sentences.zh: 龜蒙少高放，通《六經》大義，尤明《春秋》。

translations.literal: Guimeng from youth was lofty and free, penetrating the great meaning of the Six Classics, especially clear in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Guimeng was proud and detached, master of the Six Classics and especially of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，一不中，往從湖州刺史張摶游，摶曆湖、蘇二州，辟以自佐。

translations.literal: He took the jinshi examination once and failed; he went to follow Huzhou Prefect Zhang Bo; Bo served successively in Hu and Su prefectures and took him on as personal aide.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the jinshi examination once, then attached himself to Zhang Bo, prefect of Huzhou; when Bo served in Hu and Suzhou in turn, Guimeng served on his staff.

sentences.zh: 嘗至饒州，三日無所詣。

translations.literal: Once he reached Raozhou; for three days he visited no one.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Raozhou he spent three days without calling on anyone.

sentences.zh: 刺史蔡京率官屬就見之，龜蒙不樂，拂衣去。

translations.literal: Prefect Cai Jing led his officials to go see him; Guimeng was displeased and shook out his robes and left.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Cai Jing brought his entire staff to visit; Guimeng was displeased, brushed off his robes, and left.

sentences.zh: 居松江甫裏，多所論撰，雖幽憂疾痛，貲無十日計，不少輟也。

translations.literal: He lived at Puli on the Song River and wrote much; though in secret grief and illness, with funds not enough for ten days, he did not slacken.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at Puli on the Song River and wrote ceaselessly; even in private grief and sickness, with scarcely ten days' provisions, he never stopped.

sentences.zh: 文成，竄稿篋中，或歷年不省，為好事者盜去。

translations.literal: When texts were finished he stuffed the drafts in a basket; sometimes for years he did not look at them, and enthusiasts stole them away.
translations.idiomatic: Finished pieces went into a basket; sometimes he left them untouched for years, and admirers stole them.

sentences.zh: 得書熟誦乃錄，讎比勤勤，硃黃不去手，所藏雖少，其精皆可傳。

translations.literal: When he obtained books he read them thoroughly before copying; collating diligently, vermilion and yellow never left his hand; though his collection was small, the refined could all be transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: He read borrowed books through before copying them, collating with red and yellow ink always in hand; his library was small, but everything in it was worth passing on.

sentences.zh: 借人書，篇帙壞舛，必為輯褫刊正。

translations.literal: Borrowing others' books, if fascicles were damaged or disordered he would certainly gather and mend them for publication.
translations.idiomatic: When borrowed volumes were torn or out of order he always repaired and corrected them.

sentences.zh: 樂聞人學，講論不倦。

translations.literal: He delighted in hearing others study and never tired of discourse.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to hear others learn and never wearied of teaching talk.

sentences.zh: 有田數百畝，屋三十楹，田苦下，雨潦則與江通，故常苦饑。

translations.literal: He had several hundred mu of fields and thirty bays of houses; the fields were painfully low, and when rain flooded they connected with the river—so he was often hungry.
translations.idiomatic: He held several hundred mu of land and thirty rooms, but the fields were low and flooded into the river every rainy season, so hunger was his frequent guest.

sentences.zh: 身畚鍤，茠刺無休時，或譏其勞，答曰：「堯、舜黴瘠，禹胼胝。

translations.literal: He himself took basket and hoe, cutting thorns without cease; some mocked his labor; he answered: "Yao and Shun were emaciated, Yu had calloused feet—
translations.idiomatic: He worked basket and hoe himself, clearing thorns without rest. When mocked for toiling he answered, "Yao and Shun grew thin, Yu's palms blistered—

sentences.zh: 彼聖人也，吾一褐衣，敢不勤乎？」

translations.literal: they were sages; I am but a cloth-coat man—how dare I not be diligent?
translations.idiomatic: they were sages. I wear only coarse cloth—how dare I be idle?

sentences.zh: 嗜茶，置園顧渚山下，歲取租茶，自判品第。

translations.literal: He loved tea and set out a garden below Guzhu Mountain, each year taking rent tea and judging its grades himself.
translations.idiomatic: He loved tea, planted a garden below Guzhu Mountain, and each year judged the tribute tea himself.

sentences.zh: 張又新為《水說》七種，其二慧山泉，三虎丘井，六松江。

translations.literal: Zhang Youxin wrote Seven Waters; of them the second was Hui Mountain spring, the third Tiger Hill well, the sixth Song River.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Youxin's Seven Waters ranked Hui Mountain spring second, Tiger Hill well third, and the Song River sixth.

sentences.zh: 人助其好者，雖百里為致之。

translations.literal: Those who aided his taste, even from a hundred li, would bring it for him.
translations.idiomatic: Friends who shared his passion would fetch water for him from a hundred li away.

sentences.zh: 初，病酒，再期乃已，其後客至，挈壺置杯不復飲。

translations.literal: At first, ill from wine, after two periods he stopped; afterward when guests came he would take the pot and set out cups but no longer drink.
translations.idiomatic: At first illness forced him off wine; after two rounds of recovery he quit entirely. When guests came he still set out pot and cups but drank no more.

sentences.zh: 不喜與流俗交，雖造門不肯見。

translations.literal: He did not like to associate with vulgar folk; even if they came to his gate he would not see them.
translations.idiomatic: He shunned vulgar company; visitors at his door were often turned away unseen.

sentences.zh: 不乘馬，升舟設蓬席，齎束書、茶灶、筆床、釣具往來。

translations.literal: He did not ride horses; he boarded boats, spread rush mats, and with bundled books, tea stove, brush bed, and fishing gear came and went.
translations.idiomatic: He never rode a horse; he sailed with rush mats, a bundle of books, a tea stove, a writing desk, and fishing tackle.

sentences.zh: 時謂江湖散人，或號天隨子、甫裏先生，自比涪翁、漁父、江上丈人。

translations.literal: Of the time they called him the Riverside Wanderer, or styled him the Heaven-Follower, the Puli Gentleman—comparing himself to the Fuling Old Man, the Fisherman, and the Old Man of the River.
translations.idiomatic: Men called him the Riverside Wanderer, or the Heaven-Follower, or the Gentleman of Puli—likening himself to the old man of Fuling, the fisherman on the river, and the riverbank elder.

sentences.zh: 寬以高士召，不至。

translations.literal: Summoned as a lofty gentleman, he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as a lofty gentleman, he did not appear.

sentences.zh: 李蔚、盧攜素與善，及當國，召拜左拾遺。

translations.literal: Li Wei and Lu Zhi had long been on good terms with him; when they held power they summoned him as Left Remembrancer.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei and Lu Zhi, his old friends, summoned him as left remembrancer when they came to power.

sentences.zh: 詔方下，龜蒙卒。

translations.literal: The edict had just been issued when Guimeng died.
translations.idiomatic: The edict had barely been issued when Guimeng died.

sentences.zh: 光化中，韋莊表龜蒙及孟郊等十人，皆贈右補闕。

translations.literal: In the Guanghua era Wei Zhuang memorialized Guimeng together with Meng Jiao and ten others, all posthumously given Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guanghua era Wei Zhuang memorialized Guimeng, Meng Jiao, and eight others, each posthumously made right remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 陸氏在姑蘇，其門有巨石。

translations.literal: The Lu clan at Gusu had at their gate a great stone.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu family at Gusu kept a great stone at their gate.

sentences.zh: 遠祖績嘗事吳為郁林太守，罷歸無裝，舟輕不可越海，取石為重，人稱其廉，號「郁林石」，世保其居云。

translations.literal: A remote ancestor Ji once served Wu as Governor of Yulin; on retiring he had no baggage; the boat was too light to cross the sea; he took stone for weight—people praised his integrity and called it the Yulin Stone; generations preserved that dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: An early ancestor, Ji, had been Yulin governor for Wu; retiring without luggage, he found his boat too light for the sea and loaded it with stone ballast. Men praised his integrity and named it the Yulin Stone; the family kept it at their home for generations.
